title: HIVE framework and research vault
text: HIVE framework and research vault Prepared for Ian Myers · 20 November 2026 · Framework revision 0.2 Purpose: build a persistent HIVE that assembles specialists, learns from verified experience, and improves its organization while keeping the research behind each choice inspectable. Start here Need Open ------ Understand the new framework The proposed HIVE framework Explore topics and independent research paths Topic-first research map See what the Google evidence changes Google evidence and the change to HIVE Compare unresolved design choices Open design decisions Review previous methods and actual results Previous research and attempted methods Give the work to local coding agents Local coding-agent handoff Follow the build sequence and acceptance gates Local build roadmap and work packages Open the visual research map HIVE_Research_Map.canvas Check software and readiness Existing software and readiness Inspect sources and original documents Primary sources and source trail · Recovered original documents What this revision changes - Make consolidation and dreaming explicit experimental components with their own state, budgets, and acceptance tests. - Preserve the earlier replay result and test the mechanisms that it did not cover: Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch → Sleep consolidation → Test sleep, replay order, expansion and distillation independently. - Keep independent specialists, shared adapters, internal experts, deterministic tools, and hybrids as live comparison paths: Independent models or shared components. - Use research topics to organize knowledge; use measured transfer and interference to choose parameter-sharing boundaries: How specialists should be grouped. - Retain all original research and methods, including negative results and untested proposals. - Build around the existing Obsidian, Studio Brain, Graphify source, Ruflo, coding harnesses, and model runtimes after local readiness checks: Existing software and readiness. Evidence convention Label Meaning ------ Primary source reviewed The cited source was inspected; its result is still the authors' result Prior artifact audited Recovered source/results were inspected; this is not a new training run Historical import Preserved prior research; current claims have not all been reverified Proposed experiment Designed here; no result is implied Metaphor Inspiration whose software translation needs a test Unresolved An evidence, implementation, or identity gap remains This package is a research and implementation specification. It contains a linked vault, source history, experiment designs, work packages, schemas, and a link/graph validator. It does not install HIVE on the PC or claim a live integrated benchmark. Use in Obsidian 1. Extract the ZIP and open its HIVE_Framework_Research_Vault folder as a vault. 2. Open this note, then the Canvas or Research Map. 3. Use Local Graph for a topic and follow links to experiments, history, decisions, and sources. 4. For integration into the existing vault, follow Vault import and historical preservation; it preserves the current vault and adjusts Canvas file paths when needed. 5. Give Local coding-agent handoff and AGENTS.md to the local lead coding agent. The design uses ordinary Markdown links and a standard JSON Canvas. No community plugin is required to read the plan. See Obsidian Graph view and JSON Canvas specification. title: The proposed HIVE framework
text: The proposed HIVE framework Design target A modular learning system whose specialists, memories, workflows, and connections can improve independently and be evaluated together. The framework keeps the previous HIVE goal and four communication channels. Its first useful capability remains orchestrating tools and models, recovering from failures, and converting recurring corrections into dependable local improvements. See Earlier architecture choices and open alternatives and SOL, Grok, and Nemotron implementation workflow. Separate four kinds of graph Graph Nodes and edges Authoritative record Purpose ------------ Research graph Topics, claims, methods, sources, experiments, disagreements Authored notes plus typed edge ledger Explain why a design exists Code graph Symbols, modules, imports, dependencies Source at a pinned revision; derived Graphify index Find affected code and reuse Execution graph Capabilities, workflows, data dependencies, budgets Versioned recipe and runtime event log Complete work Neural structure Layers, experts, adapters, parameters Exact model/checkpoint manifest Perform learned computation Edges can connect these graphs through stable IDs. Their meanings remain explicit: a document link cannot by itself change a model or authorize a tool. Ruflo adapter where useful Communities and local recruitment Local supervisors Detect stalls and apply bounded repairs Watchdogs plus repair rules Local supervisors and intervention learning Memory service Keep ownership, dates, source lineage, and retrieval Existing Studio Brain adapter plus explicit record types Memory compartments and promotion Evidence service Distinguish observations, inferences, claims, and synthetic data Provenance records and task checkers Evidence and contradictions Learning workbench Produce candidate memory, routing, procedure, or parameter changes Isolated, reproducible jobs Wake memory–Learning and intentional forgetting Release registry Bind compatible code, model, adapter, translator, and schema versions Atomic version manifest and rollback pointer Learning and release contracts Research interface Make the design and its disputes navigable Obsidian, Canvas, derived Graphify index Obsidian and Graphify Preserve the four channels Channel Carries Explicit separation --------- Control Selection, budgets, leases, cancellation Runtime checks authority Task Domain data, requests, intermediate outputs Valid transport does not establish truth Evidence Observation, source, outcome, uncertainty A claim retains its source and conditions Teaching Proposed examples, corrections, candidate updates Admission and evaluation precede promotion A typed envelope may carry a precise text explanation, a numerical array, a scene graph, or an artifact pointer. Choose the representation for its consumer: Language or native representation. What can change Let the system state be: $$ S_t=(K_t,\Pi_t,\Theta_t,G_t,P_t,B_t) $$ Symbol Meaning Example update --------- K External knowledge and experience Add a dated correction Pi Procedures and routing policy Compile a recurring repair Theta Model and adapter parameters Train a specialist candidate G Execution connections and communities Test a new grouping P Protocols and translators Version a representation bridge B Resource allocations Change concurrency admission Every improvement record names the changed component. Better retrieval, a new script, and a trained neural model are distinct outcomes. Learning lifecycle mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [] -- Wake Wake -- Capture: verified experience Capture -- Candidate: learning need and budget Candidate -- Consolidate Candidate -- Dream Dream -- Filter Filter -- Consolidate Consolidate -- Evaluate Evaluate -- Promote: gates pass Evaluate -- Preserve: fails or uncertain Promote -- Wake Preserve -- Wake This is the proposed HIVE lifecycle. Global sleep, per-specialist sleep, and continuous updates remain comparison arms in When HIVE should sleep. A serving specialist may continue while a separate candidate learns only when the resource and compatibility tests support it. Architecture boundaries that stay flexible - A role does not require a separate full model. - A logical expert may be a program, head, adapter, checkpoint, or validated workflow. - Model count and active concurrency are measured variables, not fixed at two. - A small baseline is an experimental starting point; it does not narrow the overall HIVE hypothesis. - Adaptive orchestration, topology, and protocol changes remain explicit research paths beyond the Google result. title: Google evidence and the change to HIVE
text: Google evidence and the change to HIVE Exact source The relevant work is The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning, linked to Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories. Related paths such as Introducing Nested Learning: A new ML paradigm for continual learning, Titans + MIRAS: Helping AI have long-term memory, Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time, Self-Adapting Language Models, and Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference remain separate. Source interpretation: the evidence supports testing offline parametric consolidation and selected synthetic practice. It does not establish the whole HIVE architecture. The correction to our earlier interpretation Earlier method What was tested What it can decide --------- Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch Identical minibatches in interleaved versus blocked order Replay scheduling in the recorded small synthetic models Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories A different learning architecture and consolidation procedure Authors' results under their reported conditions Test sleep, replay order, expansion and distillation independently New controlled comparisons of the constituent mechanisms What transfers to a local HIVE workload The earlier blocked-replay result remains useful. Extending it into a rejection of sleep, expansion, distillation, or dreaming would be unsupported. New framework work Component Candidate behavior to implement Required comparison --------- Learning journal Preserve verified experience and corrections Raw retrieval and current-data baseline Consolidation worker Produce a new stable memory or skill artifact Interleaved replay and equal-capacity controls Dream worker Propose unusual but checkable training tasks Verified real replay and random synthetic examples Capacity manager Track additions, compression, and retirement Fixed-capacity and declared-growth curves Release gate Check retained quality and compatibility No-change serving baseline Sleep scheduler Allocate learning time under live workload Whole-system, staggered, and idle-only operation These are HIVE engineering proposals: Sleep consolidation, Dreaming and curriculum, Sleep without interrupting service, and Test sleep, replay order, expansion and distillation independently–Compare whole-system and per-specialist sleep during real service. Keep contrary evidence visible Independent implementation: everrete/llm-sleep records an independent implementation with a reported negative comparison and implementation gaps. Preserve it as a replication lead; inspect its choices before interpreting a failure as a verdict on the paper. Paper fidelity versus an engineering analogue Label Requirement ------ Exact reproduction attempt Pinned paper version, resolved algorithm, matching architecture/data/evaluation, deviations enumerated Partial reproduction Reproduces a specified component or result only Sleep-inspired HIVE prototype Tests an adapted mechanism on HIVE tasks and hardware New HIVE extension Adds per-specialist scheduling, graph changes, or other mechanisms outside that source claim All four are useful. Record the correct label. The first local prototype should be described as an analogue until fidelity is established. Frontier questions - Causal modularity - Developmental specialization - Event-driven and neuromorphic computation - Economic resource allocation - Metamorphic and compositional testing - Surprise and curriculum selection Done for one research pass - A precise question with at least two meaningful approaches. - A source-backed claim and its limits, or an explicit unresolved evidence gap. - A test that could distinguish the approaches. - At least one adjacent research avenue with a reason for relevance. - Links to prior methods, an experiment, and a decision. - A bounded next action with an owner, inputs, and expected artifact. “Not yet investigated” is a useful status. It must not be converted into “does not work.”

title: Evidence, disagreements, and research state
text: Evidence, disagreements, and research state Two independent status fields Evidence status Implementation status ------ Primary-source statement Not implemented Author-reported measurement Specified Independent replication report Prototype Prior artifact audited Reproduced locally Current local measurement Evaluated Hypothesis or metaphor Serving candidate Unresolved or historical import In use under named conditions A repository can be installed without having a valid benchmark. A paper can be credible without fitting this PC. Preserve alternatives without assigning equal evidence Each decision page records: - The precise question and scope. - All retained alternatives. - Evidence supporting and challenging each alternative. - A provisional implementation default. - The experiment that could change the default. - Conditions for reopening a dormant path. - A dated log explaining every change. Use statuses: unexplored, specified, testing, supported under conditions, challenged under conditions, inconclusive, dormant. Keep dormant pages linked. Claim and result records Record Required fields ------ Source Canonical URL or original file hash, authors/project, date, version, access date Claim Exact proposition, scope, source locator, observed versus inferred Experiment Hypothesis, arms, data split, budgets, seeds/orders, acceptance criteria Run Code/config/model/data hashes, hardware, timestamps, raw outputs, failures Result Metrics, variability, limitations, supported scope, counterexamples Decision Alternatives, provisional choice, rationale, reopening condition Model confidence is not a substitute for any of these fields. Disagreement example Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch and Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories differ in architecture and learning procedure. Link them with different_scope, not automatically contradicts. Sleep clearance: preserve a live disagreement preserves a biological disagreement. Compare methods and endpoints before choosing whether the findings conflict. Relationship vocabulary Relation Meaning ------ subtopic_of Research hierarchy motivated_by Analogy or inspiration supported_by Evidence supports a specific scoped claim challenged_by Evidence challenges the same relevant claim different_scope Apparently opposing results test different conditions tested_by Experiment evaluates a path or decision derived_from Historical lineage depends_on Implementation dependency adjacent_to Promising connection awaiting investigation related_to Navigation only; no evidential force The included graph uses these labels. Ordinary hyperlinks remain navigational and must not be silently interpreted as support. Import policy Historical catalogs are retained and linked. Their “succeeded,” “failed,” or similar labels remain historical classifications, not fresh HIVE measurements or current project-health judgments. Use Inherited assumptions and disputed conclusions before adopting an old recommendation.

title: Open design decisions
text: Open design decisions A build needs provisional choices. Research needs the alternatives to remain visible. Decision Experiment ------ Independent models or shared components Compare generalists, independent specialists, adapters and hybrids Where learning should persist Test bounded memory, correction, retention and removal When HIVE should sleep Compare whole-system and per-specialist sleep during real service Replay or dreaming Test whether dreaming adds value beyond verified replay Central or distributed control Scale 100, 1,000 and 10,000 logical experts with measured active workers Language or native representation Compare typed messages, precise prose and learned representations How specialists should be grouped Use measured interference to test regrouping and routing Growth, compression, and scale Scale 100, 1,000 and 10,000 logical experts with measured active workers How far self-improvement may reach Test bounded memory, correction, retention and removal Knowledge and runtime storage Reproduce prior simulations and separate estimates from measurements What constitutes verification Test whether dreaming adds value beyond verified replay How evidence changes a decision Reproduce prior simulations and separate estimates from measurements Decision rule 1. Define the workload and resource envelope. 2. Compare the retained alternatives using the named experiment. 3. Prefer a branch for those conditions, with uncertainty and tradeoffs visible. 4. Preserve the other branches and their strongest evidence. 5. Reopen after a relevant new result, implementation improvement, workload change, or resource change. No branch is erased solely because the current prototype uses another one.

title: Previous research and attempted methods
text: Previous research and attempted methods What was recovered The package preserves 19 original project artifacts, a linked history page for each source document, 12 method-history pages, and navigable entries from the prior 100-project catalog. See Recovered original documents and Prior 100-project research catalog. What the artifact audit establishes - 32 archived experiment manifest entries matched recorded file hashes and byte counts. - Raw records document 360 small NumPy learning runs and 1,440 scheduling simulations. - Central statistics were recalculated from the recorded JSON. - The experiment training scripts were not rerun during this preparation. - These artifacts do not document real-model tests on the user's RTX 5070 Ti. Findings that affect the new plan Prior result Implication Follow-up --------- Conflicting tasks: mixed two-expert grouping 66.11%, compatible grouping 83.88% Organization deserves direct testing Specialist grouping, sharing, and interference → Use measured interference to test regrouping and routing Mostly shared tasks: generalist 91.03%, isolated experts 87.00% Sharing can help; isolation is not a universal winner Specialist grouping, sharing, and interference → Independent models or shared components Conflicting generalist: interleaved replay 74.47%, blocked replay 62.64% Keep the negative scheduling result within its tested scope Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch → Test sleep, replay order, expansion and distillation independently Precise prose and precise numerical formats preserved all tested geometric labels Precision and representation are separate variables Representation precision and communication cost → Compare typed messages, precise prose and learned representations A stale translator lost accuracy after encoder drift Version bridges and test consumers together Private representations and translator drift → Learned codes and translators Well-formed semantic errors passed typed gates Syntax and authority checks do not establish truth Typed messages, authority, and semantic errors → Executable verification Scheduler studies used 4/8/16 workers Larger registry scales remain new experiments Model size, resource budgets, and larger hive scales → Scale 100, 1,000 and 10,000 logical experts with measured active workers All percentages are historical synthetic-task outcomes. Conditions and limitations are on the linked pages and in the original report. Method pages - Prior HIVE corpus and evidence lineage - Specialist grouping, sharing, and interference - Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch - Scheduling, selective activation, and graph topology - Representation precision and communication cost - Private representations and translator drift - Typed messages, authority, and semantic errors - Earlier architecture choices and open alternatives - SOL, Grok, and Nemotron implementation workflow - Video, studio interaction, and horror testbeds - Inherited assumptions and disputed conclusions - Model size, resource budgets, and larger hive scales Preserve the research lineage Initial concept → architecture → source foundation → synthetic experiments → v0.1 build/training plan → SOL handoff → this revision. A newer page can narrow or revise a conclusion while retaining the earlier page and the reason for the change.

Audit and reproduce the historical small tests: Reproduce prior simulations and separate estimates from measurements. 2. Measure the PC and existing applications: Measure the actual computer and concurrent workload. 3. Run one task family across strong generalist, independent, adapter, and hybrid baselines: Compare generalists, independent specialists, adapters and hybrids. 4. title: Local coding-agent handoff
text: Local coding-agent handoff Mission Implement the HIVE framework and research workflow in this vault using the user's existing local software. Preserve prior work, keep alternatives visible, and produce measured results rather than architecture claims inferred from a successful demo. First instruction to the lead agent Read The proposed HIVE framework, Local build roadmap and work packages, Existing software and readiness, SOL, Grok, and Nemotron implementation workflow, and AGENTS.md. Inspect the actual PC and current repositories. Create a scoped working copy or Git worktree. Do not overwrite the existing Obsidian vault or modify archived evidence. Team roles carried forward Role Intended agent Work --------- Lead and integrator SOL Architecture, contracts, backlog, dependency order, integration, evidence-based acceptance Connector implementer and reviewer Grok Tool interfaces, runtime adapters, source import, Graphify/Studio Brain wiring Contract and reliability implementer NVIDIA Nemotron Schemas, capability manifests, event state, supervision, evaluation helpers Research worker Any verified available agent One topic/path at a time; supporting, contrary, and adjacent evidence Independent evaluator Agent not responsible for the change, plus deterministic checks Inspect the actual artifacts and reproduce relevant outcomes These are assigned roles, not claims that those endpoints are currently configured. Discover exact model IDs, invocation, tool support, and locality. A local CLI may use hosted inference; record the actual provider and execution arrangement. Parallel work contract - Give every worker one bounded ticket, owned paths, input hashes, output artifacts, budget, and acceptance criteria. - Use separate worktrees for code changes; no worker writes into another's worktree. - Use a single integrator for canonical notes, registry changes, and merged results. - Let researchers submit proposed source/claim records; admission checks keep them distinct from accepted evidence. - Reassign roles according to measured capabilities, with the change recorded. - Keep SOL/Grok/Nemotron instructions portable across the installed harnesses rather than inventing unsupported CLI flags. First local ticket Ticket W00: recover the current machine state. Input Required check ------ Existing vault Confirm D:/MIcroMillionaire and current conventions Studio Brain Read-only smoke test with a known source and locator Graphify source Exact revision, dependency environment, entrypoint, output format, semantic provider Ruflo Current MCP schema and a bounded routing test Ollama / LM Studio Model inventory, one inference, cold/warm timing, memory Training candidate Compatible trainable checkpoint, forward/backward step, save/reload parity Named coding agents Exact reachable model and provider; tools and budget OBS/cameras Foreground RAM/VRAM and latency baseline Output: a dated environment manifest, a list of blocked dependencies, and the next executable tickets. Keep credentials out of the manifest. Research worker instruction For the assigned topic, read its history before searching. Create separate paths for meaningful alternatives. Collect primary evidence, counterevidence, failure boundaries, implementations, and an adjacent field. Give every claim a source and scope. Propose an experiment whose result could change the decision. Never mark a proposal as an executed trial. Completion record for each ticket - What changed and why. - Exact artifacts and versions. - What was actually executed. - Measured outcomes and failures. - Which hypothesis or decision changed. - Remaining alternatives and reopening conditions. - Next dependent ticket. User review surface The user should be able to open one decision page and follow its claim to the primary source, prior method, experiment specification, raw run, and current implementation. Graphify and knowledge adapters defines this navigation.

title: Terms and measurements
text: Terms and measurements Terms that must stay distinct Term Meaning in this framework ------ Expert A bounded capability with a contract; may be neural or non-neural Agent A process that chooses or carries out actions Internal MoE expert A neural module inside a model Adapter A compatible parameter update attached to a base model Weight update A numerical change to trained parameters Memory update A change to external stored information Sleep A named consolidation phase with specified operations Dream A marked synthetic training candidate Graphify index Derived relationships used for discovery/retrieval Obsidian graph Navigation among linked notes Evidence A sourced observation or result, with conditions Metaphor Inspiration for a mechanism; not proof Reproduction Running a specified implementation and evaluation Artifact audit Inspecting preserved code/data and recalculating records Four expert counts $$ N_{registered},\quad N_{resident},\quad N_{active},\quad N_{trainable} $$ Measure each independently. A large registry and a small active set can coexist. Measure learning, retention, and lifetime cost For a protected task i: $$ F_i=A_{before,i}-A_{after,i} $$ Positive F means forgetting in this comparison. Also report each domain, the worst protected domain, and gains on the new task. For a new task: $$ \Delta A_{new}=A_{after,new}-A_{before,new} $$ Report total examples, repeated presentations, teacher calls, synthetic candidates, discarded generations, updates, wall time, peak memory, and retained storage. Resource envelope $$ V_{peak}=V_{other\ apps}+V_{weights}+V_{cache}+V_{activations}+V_{runtime}+V_{margin} $$ All terms must be measured or explicitly labeled estimates. Training fit cannot be inferred from inference fit. Decision objective Compare the Pareto tradeoff between quality, retention, latency, learning cost, storage, and human intervention. Set application-specific constraints before confirmatory runs: $$ Q\ge Q_{min},\quad F\le F_{max},\quad L_{95}\le L_{max},\quad V_{peak}\le V_{budget} $$ Pilot gates may begin with the earlier plan's proposed quality/forgetting targets, but they are not achieved results. Lock them before the confirmatory test and retain nonattaining runs.

Keep these decisions separate: - Which model can serve the existing workload. - Which compatible checkpoint can actually be trained. - Which engine can load a candidate adapter or model version. - Which model is best under measured quality and resource limits. The default HIVE runtime and research records stay local; use existing remote coding/teacher routes only within their already configured scope. title: Vault import and historical preservation
text: Vault import and historical preservation Preferred first import Open this package as a separate Obsidian vault. This preserves existing notes and gives the local agents a bounded area to work in. To integrate into the existing vault: 1. Confirm its current path and take a normal local backup or versioned snapshot. 2. Create a new HIVE research subfolder without replacing unrelated notes. 3. Copy the package's content into that subfolder. 4. Keep relative Markdown links intact. 5. Prefix file-node paths inside the Canvas with the subfolder path, because Canvas paths are relative to the containing vault root. 6. Run the included validator against the package root; then verify Canvas navigation in Obsidian. Original evidence The 19 recovered originals are copied without changing their bytes. Recovered original documents records original names, safe archive names, and SHA-256 hashes. The long project catalog has separate navigation cards while its complete source remains preserved. Historical note content may contain old citations or platform-specific links that no longer resolve. Its wrapper records that fact; the new plan's generated internal links are checked separately. Ongoing imports Step Output ------ Preserve original Immutable bytes and hash Extract text Derived file with tool/version and extraction limits Identify claim Scoped proposition and exact source locator Link history Earlier method, decision, or experiment Add interpretation Separate current note, never silently rewrite the original Admit to graph Explicit relationship and evidence status Do not train on every imported note. Historical plans, failed proposals, synthetic examples, and accepted observations have different roles. Source history pages Every recovered document has its own wrapper page with links to relevant methods, topics, and the original file. This is the first navigation layer; the method pages explain what changed across documents.

title: Graphify and knowledge adapters
text: Graphify and knowledge adapters Responsibilities Surface Owns Must not silently imply --------- Obsidian Authored research notes, decisions, navigation A linked claim is true Graphify Derived code/document relationships for retrieval An inferred relation is evidence Studio Brain Existing vault retrieval interface Every retrieved note is current Runtime event store Executed tasks and outcomes A proposed experiment was run Model registry Exact serving and candidate artifacts A note edit retrained a model Graphify's official source describes deterministic AST code analysis and model-assisted semantic processing for some document/media inputs. Check the locally installed revision and provider configuration: Graphify official repository. Adapter contract to implement Operation Required result ------ inventory Supported formats, version, entrypoint, provider/locality ingest(snapshot) Input hashes, index revision, skipped/error records query(question, filters) Node IDs, source paths, locators, relation type, derivation neighbors(node_id) Typed edges with provenance invalidate(source_hash) Stale derived records identified export(snapshot) Rebuildable nodes and edges These are HIVE interface requirements, not claims that Graphify exposes commands with these names. Initial workflow - Inspect D:/External Tools/graphify and its checked-out instructions. - Smoke-test on a small source subset. - Confirm whether document processing can run through a configured local model. - If it cannot, keep raw-note and deterministic code paths usable while recording the semantic path as unavailable. - Preserve Graphify's extracted/inferred distinction and HIVE's claim status separately. - Compare retrieval against simple filename/text search and direct links. - Rebuild after source changes; never trust a stale index without its source revision. First graph questions - Which prior experiment actually tested this claim? - Which result challenges the preferred method? - Which metaphor motivated this implementation? - Which code modules implement the mechanism? - Which task and resource assumptions would reopen the decision?

title: Runtime and capability contracts
text: Runtime and capability contracts Minimal deterministic kernel Implement task identity, dependency tracking, deadlines, leases, cancellation, idempotent completion, bounded retries, and append-only events. Reuse existing coordination through an adapter where it satisfies the contract. A minimal local event store can use SQLite. Keep its schema and API small enough to replace later if measurements require a different backend. Capability manifest Field Required meaning ------ capability_id and version Stable identity and exact revision kind Tool, model, adapter, head, workflow, or supervisor input/output schema Versioned task contract prerequisites Models, files, services, units, and environment executor Actual verified invocation adapter model lineage Base/tokenizer/adapter/quantization compatibility when applicable resources Measured peak and configured admission limits verification Checker, supported scope, abstention condition memory scopes Read/write ownership artifact hashes Executable, weights, configuration, and supporting data Event state mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [] -- Queued Queued -- Leased Leased -- Running Running -- Checking Checking -- Completed: valid Checking -- Retryable: repair permitted Running -- Retryable: recoverable fault Retryable -- Queued: budget remains Running -- Failed: terminal fault Queued -- Cancelled Running -- Cancelled Test lease expiry, worker restart, duplicate callbacks, cancellation, and a verifier rejection. Exactly-once side effects cannot be assumed from a queue label; use operation-specific idempotency and reconciliation. Protocol envelope Required fields: schema version, task/run ID, channel, producer, target, representation version, units when relevant, source/artifact references, timestamps, and declared operation. Keep outputs in named artifact files and use hashes/pointers for large payloads. A result may include a concise explanation without transmitting every agent's entire conversation.

title: Topic-based research-agent workflow
text: Topic-based research-agent workflow One bounded research ticket Field Requirement ------ Topic and path Existing node or justified new node Question Specific mechanism and outcome Scope Workloads, models, resource assumptions, date window History Prior HIVE source/method links Search lanes Direct, competing, boundary, adjacent, implementation Budget Time, source count, tool calls, or compute cap Outputs Source cards, claims, unresolved questions, experiment proposal Review Independent source check and link validation Source collection Prefer original papers, author repositories, official documentation, released artifacts, and direct measurements. Use commentary as a lead to its underlying source. Record preprint version and repository commit. A newly published blog may describe older research; store both dates. Expansion rule For each path, ask: - What other mechanism could produce the same result? - Under what conditions would this approach fail? - Which field studies the same constraint? - Which variable have we held fixed without evidence? - What can be implemented with existing local software? - What result would change our mind? Create a separate linked path when the mechanism, assumptions, or discriminating experiment meaningfully differ. Otherwise add evidence to the existing page. Stopping rule End a research pass when it produces a reviewable decision or a clearly specified evidence gap with a next action. More notes are not the success metric. Synthesis rule Keep original claims, interpretation, and recommended experiment separate. A reviewer checks source accuracy; the lead decides implementation priority. Neither deletes alternatives to make the graph appear conclusive. Update rule A new source adds a versioned claim or revision. It may supersede a conclusion for named conditions. Retain the previous conclusion and the evidence that changed it.

title: Benchmark and measurement plan
text: Benchmark and measurement plan The three application laboratories Laboratory Frozen first task set Quality Operational measures ------------ Video Existing media jobs and recorded failures Valid artifacts, correct metadata/queue state Completion time, repeat failures, human corrections Calls and streaming Recorded interactions under normal OBS load Correct relevant response and recovery First useful response, silence, p50/p95, interruptions, dropped frames Horror haunt Reproducible room/scene and encounter states Spatial correctness, goal completion, recovery Frame/step latency, map drift sensitivity, prediction error Use one lab as the initial vertical slice while keeping the others available as transfer tests. The first choice follows measured availability, not an invented assumption about which app is already integrated. Comparison discipline - Baselines receive equivalent tools, evidence, retrieval, feedback, and fallback access. - Equal token counts do not imply equal computation. - Record training, verification, routing, translation, discarded candidates, and model loading. - Separate fixed-capacity results from growth-allowed results. - Use chronological corrections and delayed retention tests. - Keep final task compositions and seeds separate from development. - Preserve timeouts, nonattainment, and failed runs. Pilot versus confirmatory evaluation Use a small smoke test to find instrumentation and interface faults. Then estimate variance and select meaningful sample sizes. Five seeds and three task orderings are a starting design from prior planning, not a universal statistical guarantee. Set quality, latency, retention, and intervention targets before the confirmatory run. Evaluate average and worst protected task performance. Required run artifact Code commit; environment lock; model/base/adapter hashes; data and split hashes; source labels; configuration; hardware; actual resource traces; seeds/orders; timestamps; raw outputs; checks; errors; metrics; and interpretation. No benchmark score enters an accepted conclusion without the corresponding run record or an explicit author-reported label.

title: Learning and release contracts
text: Learning and release contracts Candidate types Candidate Changed artifact Required retained behavior --------- Memory consolidation Versioned external records/index Source lineage and corrections preserved Procedural learning Tool, rule, or workflow Repeated failure fixed without unrelated regressions Routing learning Selector policy/model Calibrated choices and bounded overhead Parametric learning Head, adapter, or model checkpoint New skill plus old-task retention Graph learning Community or routing configuration Useful composition under held-out tasks Protocol learning Representation/translator Compatible downstream behavior Candidate sequence 1. Snapshot serving artifacts and task fixtures. 2. Declare the changed component and hypothesis. 3. Generate or select training material with provenance. 4. Run the bounded candidate update. 5. Evaluate new-task gains, retained tasks, costs, and interface compatibility. 6. Preserve the result whether it passes or fails. 7. Promote the exact tested artifact set when the declared gates pass. 8. Roll back to a compatible known version if serving checks regress. Data and capacity accounting Count all weights, adapters, replay records, embeddings, indexes, external archives, provenance, and rollback copies when claiming bounded total storage. A bounded RAM/VRAM experiment may allow persistent storage growth, but must report it and use a different claim. See Test bounded memory, correction, retention and removal. Foreground isolation Training operates on a candidate artifact, not a live mutable serving checkpoint. The user-facing worker can keep running through another compatible artifact only if resource admission and workload tests permit it. Scope of self-improvement The foundation can learn memory and procedures early. Router, adapter, backbone, graph, and protocol changes have independent experimental paths. This preserves the stronger HIVE goal while making each improvement attributable and reversible.

title: Proposed repository and interfaces
text: Proposed repository and interfaces Suggested boundaries Adapt these to an existing repository; do not reorganize a working project without a reason. Area Content ------ docs/research This vault and source/decision records contracts Schemas and compatibility checks runtime Scheduler, task state, admission, cancellation capabilities Manifests and executor adapters memory Scoped stores and provenance supervisors Health monitoring and bounded repairs learning Candidate training, replay, dreams, consolidation evaluation Fixtures, metrics, comparison harness integrations Studio Brain, Graphify, Ruflo, media, audio, game registry Artifact versions and deployment pointers runs Immutable run manifests, raw outputs, summaries Interfaces to implement Proposed interface Meaning ------ capability.discover Return verified available capabilities task.submit / cancel / inspect Durable execution control memory.query / propose / supersede Evidence-preserving knowledge operations research.query / link / export Typed research graph operations candidate.create / evaluate Controlled experimental update release.promote / rollback Switch exact compatible artifact versions workload.measure Collect application and resource traces These are design contracts, not commands known to exist in the user's installed tools. Included support files - AGENTS.md: local implementation and research rules. - tools/validate_vault.py: check generated links, node IDs, edge references, Canvas file references, and preserved source hashes. - schemas/research_node.schema.json and research_edge.schema.json. - schemas/capability_manifest.schema.json and experiment_record.schema.json. - 99_Data/research_graph.json: portable node/edge export. - Templates for research paths, source claims, experiments, decisions, and run records. Definition of the first completed release One existing daily workflow improves under measured conditions; its repeated corrections produce a checked durable improvement; old behavior is retained within declared limits; the user can trace the change to source, history, experiment, and artifact; and competing research paths remain accessible.

title: Reproduce prior simulations and separate estimates from measurements
text: Reproduce prior simulations and separate estimates from measurements Status: prior artifacts recovered; the additional reproduction protocol below is proposed. Recovered inventory: 32 matching manifests, 360 learning records, and 1,440 scheduler records. Preserve these existing records; do not describe the entire history as unrun. Hypothesis Recorded simulation conclusions survive exact reconstruction; their dependence on assumptions can be measured separately. Evidence classes Record type What it can establish ------ Recovered manifests and numerical records Recorded configuration/output provenance Exact rerun of original NumPy/code Reproducibility of the recorded simulation Analytical estimate Consequences of stated assumptions and equations Executed model benchmark Behavior of the identified real models and workload Proposal without an execution artifact A research idea; no invented trial result Procedure 1. Start from the recovered originals and their hashes; link the 32-manifest/360-learning/1,440-scheduler inventory. 2. Rerun the original code, configuration, task order and seeds before changing anything. 3. Compare outputs using a declared numerical tolerance and the original measurement definitions. 4. Keep repairs in a new version with a change log; never overwrite the original record. 5. Run changed-assumption sensitivity trials as a separate experiment family. Outcomes, falsifier and revisit Outcome Interpretation ------ matched_original_configuration_reproduced Original conditions and outputs agree matched_original_configuration_failure Exact original conditions can run, but outputs disagree beyond tolerance changed_assumption_sensitivity Different assumptions change results; this is not a failed original reproduction blocked_reproduction Required code/data/environment is unavailable; no conclusion about reproducibility yet - Falsifier: a claimed robust ranking reverses under relevant plausible assumptions, or an exact rerun contradicts its recorded result. - Revisit: missing artifacts arrive, a bug is found, or real measurements replace simulated costs. Runs and outputs - Pilot: exact original seeds/order; deterministic calculations need no artificial seed replicates. - Confirmation of sensitivity claims: three task orders × five seeds where stochastic, adjusted after variance/power assessment. - Save original/corrected hashes, environment lock, commands, output comparisons, assumption tables and outcome labels. - Simulation reproduction establishes simulation behavior; real-model capability needs its own evidence. Related research paths Obsidian and Graphify · Branching literature discovery · Fair comparison and replication · Research-system improvement Related decisions Knowledge and runtime storage · How evidence changes a decision

title: Measure the actual computer and concurrent workload
text: Measure the actual computer and concurrent workload Status: proposed; not run. Starting inventory is user-reported RTX 5070 Ti, 64 GB DDR4, OBS, filters, videos, overlays and three cameras. Verify exact hardware and installed software locally. Hypothesis The useful HIVE operating point changes materially between an idle PC and the user's real streaming workload. Arms Workload Purpose ------ Idle operating system Reference resource envelope Normal OBS/camera scene Real daily contention OBS plus model inference Serving capacity OBS plus inference and background learning Interference and scheduling limit Procedure 1. Record device identity, usable VRAM/RAM, drivers, OS, power settings, disk and available runtimes. 2. Replay the same representative scene and audio sequence; record both cold-load and warm behavior. 3. Sweep model size, context, batch size and active workers within measured headroom. 4. Increase one resource consumer at a time; checkpoint interrupted learning jobs. 5. Retain the full latency/resource frontier instead of choosing a model by size alone. Measures and falsifier - Peak/resident VRAM and RAM; model load time; throughput; p50/p95/p99 response latency. - Audio underruns; first audible response; interruption recovery; OBS render/encode lag and dropped frames. - Learning wall time, sustained temperature/power where measurable, and disk growth. - Falsifier: a supposedly viable configuration misses the predeclared live-service limits repeatedly. - Revisit: workload, driver, model, quantization, context or available hardware changes. Runs and outputs - Pilot: a short scene replay and one learning micro-batch per candidate. - Confirmation: three workload orders × five runs; stochastic seeds apply to generated tasks, not hardware facts. Extend only when variance warrants it. - Save: verified inventory, scene/config hashes, timestamped telemetry, inference traces and feasible operating envelopes. Related research paths Local supervisors and intervention learning · Admission and residency · Video production and posting · Live calls and supervisor streaming · Horror haunt game Related decisions Open design decisions

title: Compare generalists, independent specialists, adapters and hybrids
text: Compare generalists, independent specialists, adapters and hybrids Status: proposed; not run. Treat architecture choices as competing branches. Hypothesis Specialization and coordination can improve task success per resource, but their communication and loading costs may erase the gain. Arms Arm Configuration ------ A One generalist with the same deterministic tools B Independent specialist checkpoints and explicit router C Shared backbone with selected specialist adapters D Hybrid: shared specialists plus independent modules where needed E Deterministic software baseline for tasks it can solve exactly Procedure 1. Use identical task definitions, allowed tools and chronological learning data. 2. Separate router mistakes from specialist mistakes; record tool results independently. 3. Run a common-resource comparison and a second frontier comparison using each arm's natural configuration. 4. Ablate routing, specialization and cross-checking separately. 5. Include unfamiliar tasks requiring abstention, escalation or composition. Measures and falsifier - Verified task completion; false confident outputs; calibration; latency; total inference and training cost. - Total stored parameters/artifacts, active parameters, model loading, context transfer and coordination overhead. - Falsifier: gains disappear at matched resources, or specialists fail to transfer/combine beyond their narrow tasks. - Revisit: new tasks, better routers or materially different backbone/adapter implementations. Runs and outputs - Pilot: small, balanced samples from video workflows, call interaction and game simulation. - Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds, subject to power analysis; keep a sealed final set and report intervals. - Count unsuccessful calls, verifier calls and retries. Record exact checkpoint/adaptor hashes, prompts and tool versions. - Save a Pareto table and failure taxonomy; do not collapse every tradeoff into one arbitrary score. Related research paths Independent specialists · Shared backbone and adapters · Internal experts and expandable memory · Deterministic and nonlanguage experts · Controller and routing · Executable verification · Critics and calibrated uncertainty · State estimation and world models · Parallel candidates and recovery · NCM and dynamical specialists · Video production and posting · Horror haunt game · Fair comparison and replication Related decisions Independent models or shared components

title: Test sleep, replay order, expansion and distillation independently
text: Test sleep, replay order, expansion and distillation independently Status: proposed; not run. This design separates data schedule, added capacity and consolidation mechanisms. It is not a reproduction claim. Hypothesis Consolidation improves retention beyond extra capacity, training examples, feedback or compute. Implementation class — declare before running - Paper-faithful candidate: specified architecture, equations, tasks and implementation choices match the selected paper version; list unresolved details before claiming a reproduction. - Partial implementation: named components are omitted or replaced; record every deviation. - HIVE analogue: external notes, agent routing or adapter workflows imitate a mechanism at system level; evaluate their own outcomes. - Research specification: Google Sleep paper. Factor A: wake-update data schedule only Value Examples available during wake updates ------ Current-only wake Current task only Interleaved wake Current and old examples mixed within batches Blocked wake Current and old examples in separate batches Offline data has a separate manifest: none, verified replay, teacher samples, or filtered synthetic. A current-only wake arm may rehearse offline; label that fact. A current-only total-learning arm cannot rehearse offline: those cells are NA. Factor B: mechanism contract Arm Updated modules and operations ------ Ordinary updates Update designated fast module F; no added slow capacity, consolidation or reset Expansion without sleep Unlock matched slow capacity S; train it by ordinary wake updates; no consolidation/reset/dreaming Matched-capacity distillation Fixed target adapter with matched storage/trainable capacity; same scheduled distillation budget; no hierarchical transfer/reset/dreaming Sleep without dreaming Fast F → slower S consolidation, then conditional reset; no synthetic rehearsal stage Full proposed sleep Same consolidation/reset plus the declared dreaming stage For parameter-learning arms, name F/S tensors, backbone freeze policy, update periods, ranks and allocated/active slots. An external-memory analogue identifies its corresponding stores instead of claiming tensor-level equivalence. Paper-style mechanism specification - Snapshot the pre-update teacher; compute but defer the fast-module update. - Build the candidate with the prospective update and added slow capacity; train only designated new parameters. - Use GKD/on-policy distillation plus LTI semantic/edit-similarity reward; log coefficients, sampling mixture and reward-model version. - Dreaming: extra random expert activation, generated candidates, selection, then specified refinement. HIVE acceptance rule: reset temporary fast slots only after retention/new-learning checks pass and the replacement checkpoint is durable. Otherwise retain the original state. Record this gate as an implementation addition. Compatibility and comparisons - Use NA, with a reason, when the required trainable modules, expert routing or data permissions are absent. - A frozen retrieval baseline has no wake-update schedule; it sits outside the factorial. - Match expansion/capacity ledgers; add reset/no-reset and objective ablations when a contrast changes several mechanisms. - Screen cheaply; confirm selected contrasts on unseen examples/orders. Preserve all screened results. Measures, falsifier and outputs - Measure before learning, after each task, after consolidation and after reset. - Count all updates, examples generated/scored/discarded, external feedback, verifier/router fanout, wall time and total stored growth. - Report fixed-compute and fixed-example comparisons separately; include old/new accuracy, corrections and serving delay. - Falsifier: gains disappear under matched controls, or reset destroys retained knowledge. Revisit: implementation gaps or changed workloads. - Pilot: one short stream. Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds by default, revised using variance/power. - Save compatibility matrix, preregistered contrasts, module/update manifest, seeds, hashes, raw scores and deviation log. Related research paths Sleep consolidation · Internal experts and expandable memory · Fair comparison and replication · Biology and physical translation Related decisions Open design decisions

title: Test whether dreaming adds value beyond verified replay
text: Test whether dreaming adds value beyond verified replay Status: proposed; not run. Keep synthetic examples, external evidence and newly acquired labels distinguishable. Hypothesis Diverse, selected synthetic exercises improve transfer beyond verified replay when compute and external feedback are controlled. Arms Arm Learning material ------ A Replay of the same verified examples already available B Random model-generated examples C Examples from unusual expert combinations D Unusual combinations plus declared selection E Newly acquired verified examples, with acquisition cost reported Arm E is a practical resource-allocation comparison. Its extra ground truth cannot support a causal claim that dreaming alone helps or harms. Two complementary controls Comparison Match and report ------ Equal compute Generation, rejection, scoring, training and verifier compute; disclose unequal external feedback Equal external feedback Same evidence/label pool and access budget; count new labels, annotation time, verifier calls and outcomes exposed to learners A verifier answer can provide new task information even when no human labels it. Record answer quality and reuse rules, not only call count. Include a combined compute/feedback-matched contrast where feasible. Procedure 1. Separate training/selection-development evidence from the sealed final test set. 2. Use executable, symbolic or independently adjudicated outcomes where possible. 3. Test familiar tasks and novel combinations of learned skills. 4. Charge discarded candidates, failed trials and per-dream updates to their generating arm. 5. Track evidence-backed, inferred and unsupported content across successive cycles. Measures and falsifier - Held-out transfer, retained skills, invalid-example rate and error amplification. - Benefit per total compute, external feedback unit and acquisition cost; diversity after selection. - Falsifier: gains vanish under equal feedback, improve only the selection metric, or amplify false claims. - Revisit: stronger verification or a different information/acquisition budget. Runs and outputs - Pilot: one verifier-grounded domain with small batches. - Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds, adjusted using variance/power; final test items never train or select. - Save candidate provenance, accept/reject reasons, feedback ledger, acquisition costs, checkpoint ancestry and raw held-out scores. - Model agreement is a signal, not ground truth. Related research paths Dreaming and curriculum · Executable verification · Critics and calibrated uncertainty · Parallel candidates and recovery Related decisions Replay or dreaming · What constitutes verification

title: Use measured interference to test regrouping and routing
text: Use measured interference to test regrouping and routing Status: proposed; not run. Communities and expert assignments are variables, not permanent assumptions. Hypothesis Regrouping experts based on observed interference and transfer outperforms fixed topic groups at equal coordination cost. Arms Arm Grouping/routing rule ------ A Fixed human-defined topic communities B Fixed similarity-based communities C Adaptive routing with fixed communities D Adaptive routing and regrouping using measured transfer/interference E Random changes at the same frequency and budget Procedure 1. Build a task-by-task transfer matrix using designated development probes. 2. Separate representational interference, router errors and shared-resource contention. 3. Trigger changes using predeclared thresholds and minimum evidence counts. 4. Charge migration, retraining, adapter loading and context translation to the changing arm. 5. Run the sealed evaluation only after freezing the candidate routing/grouping version. Measures and falsifier - Cross-task interference; positive transfer; route regret; success rate; switching/migration cost. - Group churn, oscillation, missed deadlines and recovery after a specialist fails. - Falsifier: gains vanish after charging reorganization, or regrouping oscillates without durable held-out benefit. - Revisit: task distribution changes or sufficient new evidence invalidates an earlier grouping. Runs and outputs - Pilot: a small set of overlapping and conflicting tasks. - Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds; keep task families separated across development and final evaluation. - Save graph snapshots, edge evidence, change triggers, routing traces and rollback checkpoints. - Preserve superseded groupings as versioned alternatives with reasons for revisiting them. Related research paths Independent specialists · Controller and routing · Adaptive graph and grouping Related decisions How specialists should be grouped

title: Compare typed messages, precise prose and learned representations
text: Compare typed messages, precise prose and learned representations Status: proposed; not run. A representation is evaluated by information preserved and actions enabled. Hypothesis Typed or learned inter-expert messages can reduce communication cost while retaining task-relevant meaning; translation and drift may offset the saving. Arms Arm Message format ------ A Precise natural language with an agreed vocabulary B Typed schemas, units, enums and explicit evidence identifiers C Domain-native objects: graphs, equations, timelines or spatial state D Learned latent messages plus a trained/versioned translator E Hybrid typed envelope with a domain-native or latent payload Procedure 1. Reuse identical source tasks and downstream decisions across arms. 2. Test missing fields, unit changes, contradictions, unseen tasks and upgraded specialists. 3. Measure end-to-end results, not compression alone. 4. For learned messages, version both encoder and decoder; test old/new combinations and round-trip meaning preservation. 5. Keep control authority and evidence provenance explicit regardless of payload format. Measures and falsifier - Task success; lost constraints; semantic/unit errors; decode cost; bandwidth; latency; cross-version failures. - Independent auditability and leakage of unrelated domain information into decisions. - Falsifier: compressed messages save tokens but increase consequential errors or fail after routine component updates. - Revisit: better translators, schema revisions or a new domain with different native structure. Runs and outputs - Pilot: constrained messages with known target meaning. - Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds; include unseen schemas/tasks and version-transition cases. - Save schemas, encoder/decoder hashes, source/decoded examples, decision traces and compatibility results. - Different representations alone do not guarantee isolation or prevent cross-contamination. Related research paths Deterministic and nonlanguage experts · Typed channels · Domain-native representations · Learned codes and translators · Contamination and boundaries · NCM and dynamical specialists · Horror haunt game · Biology and physical translation Related decisions Language or native representation

title: Test bounded memory, correction, retention and removal
text: Test bounded memory, correction, retention and removal Status: proposed; not run. Separate bounded total storage from bounded live serving memory. External archives are never off-ledger. Hypothesis Selective consolidation can preserve useful learning and correction behavior under a declared resource regime. Two distinct resource regimes Regime What is bounded Required report --------- Total-system persistent cap All weights, adapters, replay data, indexes, archives, provenance, checkpoints and rollback copies Total bytes by category; quota use; temporary write headroom; behavior at saturation Bounded serving footprint Live RAM/VRAM; persistent disk may grow Peak/resident serving memory and cumulative total persistent bytes/growth rate For the strict cap, reserve write/rollback headroom inside the quota. If provenance or rollback retention prevents further learning, report the resulting stop/degradation rather than silently exceeding the cap. Arms within each applicable regime - Add modules until the cap, then stop growth. - Merge/distill modules with measured consolidation costs. - Evict by a declared utility rule. - External archive plus retrieval, charged to total persistent storage. - Hybrid archive plus compact learned modules. Mark an arm NA when it cannot meet the specified regime. Do not compare an unbounded archive against bounded storage as if capacities matched. Procedure 1. Introduce dated synthetic facts, unrelated skills and contradictory claims. 2. Replace selected facts; test current answers and explicitly historical queries separately. 3. Remove designated synthetic canary facts from affected serving/training artifacts; record which copies remain. 4. Probe direct, paraphrased and compositional access after updates and restarts. 5. Continue beyond repeated saturation/correction cycles; log every store and temporary peak. Measures and falsifier - Total persistent bytes, live RAM/VRAM, archive growth, update/retrieval costs and new/old performance. - Correction uptake, obsolete-answer rate, canary recovery and provenance completeness. - Distinguish retrieval deletion from reducing information's influence in model parameters. - Falsifier: claimed bounded learning relies on off-ledger growth, stalls at saturation, or only hides obvious removal queries. - Revisit: new management methods, a changed cap or stronger removal tests. Runs and outputs - Pilot: synthetic facts with small explicit quotas. - Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds through repeated saturation, adjusted using variance/power and trend uncertainty. - Save category-level capacity ledger, checkpoint ancestry, correction/removal manifests, raw probes and trajectories. - Report observed removal behavior; limited tests do not establish universal unlearning. Related research paths Wake memory · Sleep consolidation · Learning and intentional forgetting · Shared backbone and adapters · Internal experts and expandable memory · Memory compartments and promotion · Evidence and contradictions · Contamination and boundaries · Video production and posting Related decisions Where learning should persist · How far self-improvement may reach

title: Compare whole-system and per-specialist sleep during real service
text: Compare whole-system and per-specialist sleep during real service Status: proposed; not run. Treat global sleep, staggered sleep and idle-only consolidation as live branches. Hypothesis Staggered or workload-aware consolidation can preserve live-call and OBS quality while still producing useful learning. Arms Arm Schedule ------ A Global sleep during a declared maintenance interval B Per-specialist sleep with a frozen serving replica or alternate route C Idle-only learning triggered by measured resource headroom D Continuous low-priority learning E Frozen serving system with no learning, as service reference Procedure 1. Replay the same call/OBS workload and incoming learning stream. 2. Include interruptions, rapid turn-taking, scene transitions and camera/filter load. 3. Define serving limits and learning freshness targets before each run. 4. Checkpoint learning jobs before preemption; promote only versioned candidates that pass evaluation. 5. Measure stale knowledge and deferred learning as well as foreground responsiveness. Measures and falsifier - First audible response, p95/p99 response latency, barge-in recovery and audio gaps. - OBS render/encode lag, dropped frames, VRAM/RAM peaks and service availability. - Consolidation throughput, queue age, knowledge freshness and retention after resuming. - Falsifier: scheduling meets latency only by indefinitely starving learning, or learning repeatedly disrupts service limits. - Revisit: changed workload, hardware, replica cost or learning duration. Runs and outputs - Pilot: recorded workload with injected interruptions. - Confirmation: three workload orders × five runs; use task seeds where stochastic and retain real-time telemetry. - Save scheduler decisions, interrupted/resumed checkpoint IDs, audio/OBS metrics and learning queue history. - A per-specialist schedule is a HIVE engineering hypothesis, not an established Google result. Related research paths Communities and local recruitment · Local supervisors and intervention learning · Admission and residency · Sleep without interrupting service · Live calls and supervisor streaming · Biology and physical translation Related decisions When HIVE should sleep

title: Scale 100, 1,000 and 10,000 logical experts with measured active workers
text: Scale 100, 1,000 and 10,000 logical experts with measured active workers Status: proposed; not run. Expert registry size, available parameter sets and simultaneously running models are different quantities. Hypothesis A large catalog of specialized roles/modules can remain useful with a smaller, dynamically scheduled active set; indexing, routing and coordination may become the bottlenecks. Arms Dimension Values to retain ------ Logical expert registry 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 entries Active workers Sweep from measured hardware feasibility; no fixed two-model cap Representation Prompts/tools / adapters / independent checkpoints / hybrid Routing Flat lookup / hierarchical routing / retrieval-assisted selection Scheduling Resident / queued / cached loading / mixed Procedure 1. Benchmark registry/index operations with synthetic entries and explicit simulated task costs. 2. Separately run real models at measured active-worker counts. 3. Populate meaningful distinct specialists for capability tests; duplicated labels do not create new expertise. 4. Measure warm and cold selection, loading, fanout, contention and failure recovery. 5. Calibrate the simulation against measured runs; mark extrapolations beyond observed conditions. Measures and falsifier - Route quality and search time; cache hit rate; queue wait; loading cost; useful concurrency. - Task success per total cost; duplicated work; cascade failures; RAM/VRAM/disk footprint. - Falsifier: larger catalogs add noise/overhead without improved held-out task coverage, or simulated gains fail in real runs. - Revisit: better indexing, distinct expert training, hardware changes or new task diversity. Runs and outputs - Pilot: synthetic scheduling sweep and a small calibrated real-model run. - Confirmation: three task orders × five seeds per selected configuration; expand with variance/power needs. - Save registry manifest, distinct capability coverage, actual active counts, simulation assumptions and real runtime traces. - Report orchestration scalability separately from intelligence or model-capability improvement. Related research paths Communities and local recruitment · Adaptive graph and grouping · Logical expert scale · Admission and residency Related decisions Central or distributed control · Growth, compression, and scale

title: Prior HIVE corpus and evidence lineage
text: Prior HIVE corpus and evidence lineage Status Recovered evidence and proposals; no new HIVE training run in this audit. - The recovered collection contains 19 original files: architecture plans, literature catalogs, software inventory, experiment bundle, figures, and application handoffs. - The November 18 foundation says the integrated HIVE system was not built. A separate November 18 experiment report subsequently records small CPU mechanism studies. These statements describe different scopes; preserve both. - November 19 documents specify v0.1 training and the SOL/Grok/Nemotron foundation workflow. A specification is not a completed implementation. Evidence levels Label Meaning here ------ Archived run Source, seed/configuration records, and results recovered Recomputed statistic This audit recalculated a value from archived JSON Reproduced experiment Reserved for a fresh execution; not claimed here Proposed Design or experiment not shown as executed Discovery lead Earlier resource catalog entry needing source verification What to preserve - Original bytes and names in the archive; corrections belong on linked notes. - Separate source, claim, experiment, decision, and implementation pages. - All competing arms and negative outcomes. - Original run environment: CPU/NumPy, no GPU and no downloaded model weights. Next path: reproduce the archived studies locally, then attach new run IDs before comparing them with real-model HIVE experiments. title: Specialist grouping, sharing, and interference
text: Specialist grouping, sharing, and interference Actually tried 360 archived NumPy MLP training runs: five seeds; three parameter budgets; four organizations; three replay schedules; two synthetic rule regimes. Every run used 360 optimizer updates and 11,520 sample presentations. At approximately 4,096 total parameters with interleaved replay: Organization Shared rules Conflicting rules ------:---: One generalist 91.03% 74.47% Two mixed pairs 89.59% 66.11% Two compatible pairs 89.80% 83.88% Four isolated experts 87.00% 88.98% Retain both findings: isolation protects conflicting skills; sharing can improve transfer when rules overlap. Regrouping the same two experts improved conflicting-task accuracy by 17.76 percentage points. Its descriptive five-seed 95% interval was ±6.75 points, without multiple-comparison correction. Boundary - Grouping and domain routing were supplied by the generator, not discovered by HIVE. - These were independent tiny networks, not pretrained LLMs or shared-backbone adapters. - No result establishes a universal best specialist count. New path Measure a transfer/interference matrix after each candidate update. Compare topic-defined groups, learned groups, independent experts, and shared adapters. Topic-first research organization should not force identical neural sharing boundaries. See replay and capacity. title: Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch
text: Replay ordering and the reopened sleep branch Actually tried The archived experiment changed the order of the same minibatches. It used a bounded 256-record replay store and an equal presentation budget. Conflicting-task generalist, ~4K parameters Final accuracy ------: Current data only 54.31% Interleaved old/new replay 74.47% Current block, then old-data block 62.64% Interleaved replay exceeded blocked replay by 11.84 percentage points; descriptive five-seed 95% interval ±5.78 points. What this result means The old-data-only tail could overwrite recent conflicting learning. Fully isolated experts produced identical interleaved/blocked results because updates did not cross their parameter boundaries. Replay also consumed budget otherwise available for fresh examples. What it did not test - Expanded specialist memory or additional low-rank experts. - Upward knowledge distillation. - Generative dreaming or curated synthetic practice. - A learned consolidation controller or biological REM. Keep the negative replay result and the new Google Sleep evidence together. They test different mechanisms; the old experiment cannot reject the larger sleep hypothesis. New path Compare matched-budget interleaving, mixed-data offline consolidation, expansion alone, distillation alone, and the full sleep recipe. Add dreaming as a separate ablation. Count extra parameters, examples, training compute, and serving disruption. title: Scheduling, selective activation, and graph topology
text: Scheduling, selective activation, and graph topology Actually tried The archived discrete-event study contains 1,440 runs and 345,600 simulated task requests. It varied 4/8/16 workers, four graph topologies, selective versus broadcast activation, locality, load, and assumed communication costs. All workers shared one serial accelerator and four CPU message-service lanes. Workers available Selective accelerator work/task Broadcast work/task ------:---: 4 2.50 units 4.01 units 8 2.47 units 8.00 units 16 2.50 units 16.00 units What survives - Available connections and activated workers are different variables. - A central scheduler can coexist with direct data exchange. - At low communication cost, the shared accelerator dominated latency; additional forwarding mattered more as message cost increased. Boundary Costs were assumed normalized units, not measured GPU timings. Broadcast was defined to await every peer without adding answer-quality benefit. Finite traces were drained after arrival stopped; overloaded results are not steady-state capacity estimates. Loading, KV caches, batching, graph maintenance, and learned routing were absent. New path Replay measured local service traces through the scheduler. Separately compare 100/1,000/10,000 registered capabilities, active worker counts, and residency policies. Preserve direct mesh, hub, community-tree, and bridge alternatives. title: Representation precision and communication cost
text: Representation precision and communication cost Actually tried Across 50,000 synthetic geometric scenes, each representation preserved or discarded coordinates used for three deterministic decisions. No images were recognized. Representation Labels retained Mean payload ------:---: Float32 binary 100.00% 32 bytes Numerical JSON 100.00% 155.02 bytes Precise coordinate prose 100.00% 171 bytes Five-bin words 86.97% 82.49 bytes Same five-bin numeric codes 86.97% 8 bytes Retain both interpretations - Compact native values can avoid textual serialization overhead. - Precise prose preserved all tested labels. The demonstrated loss came from quantization, not from English itself. The binary payload was approximately 4.84 times smaller than JSON. This is a payload-byte comparison, excluding headers and transport; it is not an inference-speed or token-speed measurement. Finite-sample perfect retention is not a guarantee for every numerical decision boundary. New path Compare precise typed text, tensors, ASTs, event streams, and captions on actual application tasks. Measure downstream correctness, reconstruction error, total bytes, encoder/translator cost, and latency. Keep user explanations readable while retaining native data where downstream consumers benefit. See translation for incompatible learned spaces. title: Private representations and translator drift
text: Private representations and translator drift Actually tried Two modules encoded identical eight-dimensional geometry using different random orthogonal coordinate systems. A 64-coefficient linear translator learned their relationship from paired examples. Ten seeds and held-out scenes were used. Condition Labels retained ------: No translator 49.91% 16 noiseless paired examples 100.00% 64 pairs with noise SD 0.02 97.84% Stale translator after encoder changed 50.26% Interpretation Equal shape and numerical type do not establish shared meaning. Good translation can restore useful information, while changing an encoder can break an otherwise working pipeline. Boundary This was fitted linear algebra in an intentionally easy low-dimensional setting. It did not test arbitrary pretrained LLM hidden states, learned private language, adversarial translation, or a universal embedding space. The training and evaluation conditions were synthetic. New path Maintain a versioned bundle of encoder, representation, translator, consumer, and stored embeddings. Compare explicit shared schemas, aligned embeddings, learned translators, and no translation. Require held-out downstream tests before activating a replacement; measure alignment-data cost and drift repair. Retain private-language research as an experimental branch. Do not use private encodings as an authorization mechanism; see message boundaries. title: Typed messages, authority, and semantic errors
text: Typed messages, authority, and semantic errors Actually tried The archive evaluated 30,000 generated messages under four deterministic gate policies. Each seed included 3,000 messages and simulated authenticated identities. Gate Invalid messages accepted Unauthorized writes accepted/seed Well-formed false semantics accepted ------:---:---: Shape only 100% 500/500 100% Typed contract 40% 500/500 100% Types + capabilities 20% 0/500 100% Types + capabilities + range 20% 0/500 100% What this establishes Types, versions, units, recipients, and scoped authority can reject the injected interface and permission errors. Range checks offered no additional benefit for this particular mixture. What remains Every well-formed semantic error passed. No real database write, cryptographic authentication, OS sandbox, or model-weight update occurred. The artificial error mixture does not estimate deployment failure rates. New path Enforce authority in the runtime and storage service. Test provenance, independent truth checks, contradiction handling, and update ownership separately. Preserve the four Control/Task/Evidence/Teaching channels, with explicit transitions between them. A successfully delivered Task message must not automatically become trusted Teaching data. See translation and SOL implementation.
