title: Earlier architecture choices and open alternatives
text: Earlier architecture choices and open alternatives Historical proposals The core architecture introduced specialist communities; immediate/domain/episodic/procedural/collective memory; replaceable components; and four communication channels. The foundation expanded this into a catalog of 100 code/model resources and 30 primary papers. Candidate Prior intended role Evidence status here --------- LAYA Routing and structured decisions Local environment prepared; service was offline Ruflo Replaceable orchestration adapter MCP routing responded in prior inventory NCM Concept-oriented processing research Proposed branch; no HIVE trial recovered Shared-base adapters Efficient specialization Proposed comparison arm Independent backbones/heads Isolated learning ownership Tiny independent MLPs tried; LLM arm not established Symbolic tools Exact calculation and verification Implementation direction; integrated result not established Preserve the choices Keep shared, independent, and hybrid organizations. Distinguish prompt roles, adapters, model backbones, deterministic tools, and memory records when counting experts. Multiple names do not establish independent reasoning or independent errors. title: SOL, Grok, and Nemotron implementation workflow
text: SOL, Grok, and Nemotron implementation workflow Prior plan, not completed execution The November 19 handoff assigns: Role Ownership ------ SOL Architecture, sequencing, integration, acceptance Grok Connectors, software interfaces, API checks, peer review NVIDIA Nemotron Contracts, memory, diagnostics, watchdogs, independent checks Each coder uses a separate Git worktree. Assignments declare allowed paths, inputs, interfaces, acceptance criteria, resource limits, reviewer, and evidence to return. Roles can be reassigned after measured capability checks. title: Printed pneumatic robots and structure doing computation
text: Printed pneumatic robots and structure doing computation - Observed mechanism: Gepner and colleagues describe a fully printed soft robot with embedded fluidic control and a standardized fabrication platform. - Software translation — proposal: Let structure carry repeated work: arithmetic through a calculator, dependencies through a graph, valid configurations through constraints, and stable procedures through finite-state or compiled workflows. A model selects and adapts these mechanisms. - Competing branches: General-model reasoning at every step; a specialist model; deterministic structure; a hybrid planner selecting structures. Keep physical morphology research as its own future branch, linked to the software experiment. - Falsifiable experiment: Hold task success criteria constant while changing where the work happens. Measure latency, failure rate, maintenance effort, and adaptation after requirements change. Structural simplification loses support if its apparent speed requires brittle assumptions that fail the changed task. - Analogy limit: Fluidic mechanics and software representations are different mechanisms. This paper is a verified physical example; the user's earlier articulated inflatable-limb reference remains separately unidentified. - Adjacent avenues: Morphological computation, fluidic logic, constraint programming, compilation, and embodied control. title: Domain signals and learned communication codes
text: Domain signals and learned communication codes - Observed precedent: Foerster and colleagues studied learned communication protocols in constrained cooperative multi-agent tasks, including differentiable communication during centralized training. - Software translation — proposal: Define separate control, task, evidence, and teaching messages. Compare natural language with typed schemas, domain-native objects, and learned latent codes. Version encoders and translators so message meaning can be traced across changes. - Competing branches: Shared human-readable language; typed symbolic messages; tensors or scene graphs; learned communication; translator specialists. Preserve all as candidates for different domains rather than requiring one universal language. - Falsifiable experiment: Replace a participant, change an encoder version, withhold a task, and drop or alter messages. Measure final task success, decoding cost, error detection, and recovery. Compact codes lose their efficiency claim if interoperability repairs outweigh their transmission savings. - Analogy limit: Independently trained models do not automatically share meaningful hidden representations. Private codes do not provide memory isolation or establish truth. - Adjacent avenues: Type systems, representation alignment, communication theory, protocol negotiation, and multi-agent learning. title: Sleep clearance: preserve a live disagreement
text: Sleep clearance: preserve a live disagreement - Evidence A: Hauglund and colleagues linked norepinephrine-driven vascular oscillations with cerebrospinal-fluid transport and clearance during mouse NREM sleep. - Evidence B: Miao and colleagues reported reduced clearance during sleep and anesthesia using fluorescent-dye measurements in male mice. - Measurement dispute: Tracers, delivery, assays, and sleep conditions differ. Hauglund also measured radiotracer clearance; the disagreement cannot be reduced to inflow versus outflow alone. Preserve both studies and their methods. - Software translation — proposal: Treat cleanup as several processes: stopping intake, moving records, removing duplicates, compressing storage, and deleting obsolete state. Measure each separately rather than calling all of them clearance. - Competing branches: Scheduled cleanup; continuous cleanup; workload-triggered cleanup; preservation with extra capacity. - Falsifiable experiment: Track incoming, retained, moved, and removed records under identical workloads. Compare correctness, storage, latency, and recoverability. Faster movement alone does not demonstrate useful removal. - Analogy limit: Conflicting biological findings do not establish which maintenance schedule software needs. - Adjacent avenues: Conservation equations, measurement validity, garbage collection, data lifecycle management, and replication design. title: Coder directions — revision 0.4
text: HIVE — Three-Conversation Information Packet for the Coder Prepared for: Ian Myers Date: 20 November 2026 Revision: 0.4 — expanded synthesis Status: Research handoff and proposed implementation specification. No new HIVE runtime or benchmark is claimed. Contents - 1. Mandate and source coverage - 2. What the three conversations add to HIVE - 3. Philosophy and mythology translated into software - 4. Odysseus and the 25-project inventory - 5. Fictional hive minds as architecture stress tests - 6. Proposed architecture and module boundaries - 7. Data contracts and learning lifecycle - 8. Build sequence and acceptance checks - 9. Decisions that remain open - 10. Research vault integration - 11. Direct instructions to the coder - 12. Sources and recovery limits 1. Mandate and source coverage Build intent HIVE is a persistent, modular, adaptive system of specialist models, deterministic software, memory, communication, and supervision. It should improve the combinations that do useful work: which specialists participate, what they receive, how they communicate, what they remember, and how their procedures and learned capabilities change. The organizing question is: How can HIVE learn which capabilities to assemble, preserve their useful differences, verify their work, and retain improvements across tasks? This packet combines the three research conversations immediately preceding the synthesis request: Source Conversation Recovered material --------- R1 Research Philosophy and Mythology Named philosophical frameworks, mental models, myths, and the main HIVE interpretations. R2 Analyze Odysseus Projects Odysseus lessons, all 25 comparison-project names and repository links, and priority mechanisms to investigate. R3 Research Hive Minds Four structural categories, three evaluation axes, six named examples, and their main failure-mode lessons. Coverage limit: Retrieved conversation excerpts support this synthesis, but the complete original transcripts were not available. The fictional comparison reportedly covered 21 systems, including five fantasy examples; its complete roster and numerical scores were not recovered. This packet preserves the available findings and leaves those scores unfilled. Evidence labels Label Use ------ Carried-forward requirement An existing user direction or requirement in the prior HIVE framework. Recovered finding An idea or conclusion present in retrieved conversation excerpts; not automatically a user-approved decision. Source checked A named external source was inspected for the particular claim. Metaphor A conceptual analogy that suggests a test. Proposed implementation A new engineering translation made in this packet. Unresolved Missing evidence or a choice that still requires measurement. The architecture, schemas, work packages, and acceptance checks below are proposed implementation. They make the research actionable without presenting every suggestion from an earlier assistant as an adopted requirement. Existing HIVE commitments to preserve The earlier framework supplies the following context: - Keep independent specialists, shared-backbone adapters, internal experts, deterministic tools, and hybrids available as comparison paths. - Preserve competing explanations, prior attempts, negative results, and the conditions under which a decision should reopen. - Keep consolidation and sleep-inspired learning as explicit research branches. Evaluate their mechanisms separately. - Organize research by topics and subtopics; use evidence about transfer and interference to choose actual specialist boundaries. - Use the existing Obsidian vault, Studio Brain, Graphify source, Ruflo, coding harnesses, and model runtimes after checking readiness. - Distinguish logical expert count, active workers, and resident models. Claims about 100, 1,000, or 10,000 experts require actual measurements. - Develop useful applications in video production, live-call/supervisor streaming, and the horror-haunt game. 2. What the three conversations add to HIVE Addition Combined reasoning Concrete implementation target --------- Remember successful combinations K-lines supplies the organizing idea; skill audits supply a validation pattern. Versioned execution recipes containing participants, dependencies, conditions, and outcome evidence. Cooperate across different representations Trading zones, language-games, and Babel highlight the difference between exchanging a message and understanding it. Typed contracts, explicit translators, provenance, units, and visible translation failures. Coordinate while retaining disagreement Pluralism and informative dissent align with fictional collectives that coordinate well but make collective mistakes. Separate candidate claims, evidence, decision ownership, and validation. Treat continuity as an explicit design choice Process philosophy, the Ship of Theseus, distributed AIs, and divided collectives raise replacement and divergence questions. Persistent identities, instance IDs, version histories, fork lineage, and reconciliation rules. Make adaptation an observable process Pragmatism, double-loop learning, and Odysseus-style auditing connect change to consequences. Candidate changes, baselines, held-out evaluation, promotion records, and rollback. Bound repair and coordination costs Hydra, near-decomposability, and communication-dependent minds expose cascading failures and connection costs. Local watchdogs, limited retries, explicit budgets, and topology benchmarks. Give local groups bounded responsibility Polycentric governance offers a way to distribute decisions without requiring identical internal beliefs. Scoped ownership, local decisions, and explicit cross-domain conflict resolution. First useful result: a task completes through a recorded combination of models and tools, survives a meaningful failure, produces independently checkable output, and creates an improvement candidate that is evaluated before reuse. 3. Philosophy and mythology translated into software 3.1 Philosophical and cognitive frameworks The names and central angles in this table were recovered from R1. The software column is an engineering interpretation, not a claim that philosophy proves a particular architecture. Framework Recovered angle Proposed HIVE consequence --------- Edwin Hutchins — distributed cognition Organization and relationships participate in cognition. Evaluate the whole arrangement of people, models, tools, memory, and procedures. Attribute gains to the arrangement being tested. Andy Clark and David Chalmers — extended mind External tools and memory can participate in cognition. Make calculators, search, files, retrieval, and software capabilities first-class components in the registry. William James — pluralism Coherence can involve partial perspectives. Preserve scoped hypotheses and disagreements; require only the coordination needed for the task. Charles Sanders Peirce — pragmatism Concepts gain meaning through practical consequences. Define “learning,” “understanding,” and “improvement” with observable task outcomes. Ludwig Wittgenstein — language-games Meaning depends on role and use. Distinguish a command, observation, hypothesis, explanation, and teaching example in message contracts. Buddhist chariot / Vajira Sutta The whole can be understood as an organized assemblage. Specify which relationships and state make HIVE function; do not require one permanent central model. Alfred North Whitehead — process philosophy Continuity can be a continuing pattern of activity. Track persistent state and lineage as components change. Marvin Minsky — Society of Mind / K-lines Recall useful configurations of resources. Store a successful execution recipe, including when it worked and when it should not be reused. Peter Galison — trading zones Groups can cooperate through limited exchange while retaining different practices. Keep specialist-local representations; validate adapters at the boundaries that need translation. Elinor Ostrom — polycentric governance Multiple centers can hold bounded authority. Give task or domain owners explicit decision rights and resource limits. Chris Argyris — double-loop learning Recurring failures may require changing the rule producing them. Allow an evaluated change to routing, workflow, or policy after repeated failures. James March — exploration and exploitation Searching for new options competes with using known ones. Maintain a working default plus a bounded budget for candidate configurations. Herbert Simon — near-decomposability Subsystems can have stronger internal than external coupling. Measure whether grouping specialists reduces coordination cost without harming capability. W. Ross Ashby — requisite variety Control must accommodate relevant variation. Test whether available responses cover observed failure classes; add a capability when evidence identifies a gap. Charlan Nemeth — informative dissent Useful dissent involves different evidence or thinking. Compare independently produced methods and evidence; measure whether a challenger adds information. 3.2 Mythological metaphors These are research labels. Use ordinary names such as execution_log, translator, and change_evaluator in the code. Metaphor recovered in R1 Useful design question Proposed behavior or test --------- Indra’s net How does a specialist’s value depend on its connections? Remove or replace selected connections and measure the effect on task outcomes. Ariadne’s thread Can exploration preserve a route back? Record parent branches, checkpoints, attempts, and outcome evidence. Resume with idempotency or effect reconciliation. Hydra and Iolaus Can a repair create more failures than it removes? Evaluate target improvement and downstream regressions; bound retry and repair-agent growth. Churning the Ocean of Milk What makes productive tension possible? Give competing approaches a shared task, exchange protocol, stable infrastructure, and common evaluation criteria. Odin’s Huginn and Muninn How should observation, recall, and interpretation relate? Keep observations distinguishable from derived memory and reasoning. Babel Did delivery also preserve meaning? Test schema, units, context, and unknown fields at each translation boundary. Janus What must a boundary check on entry and exit? Validate incoming scope and outgoing provenance; prevent unsupported promotion between memory compartments. Ship of Theseus What persists as components are replaced? Preserve identity, lineage, and historical attribution through model, tool, and memory upgrades. Ma’at’s scales and Thoth’s record Who states a claim, applies a standard, evaluates it, and records the result? Keep output, evaluation criteria, verifier evidence, and audit record distinct. Mythology qualification preserved from the conversation: both of Odin’s ravens gather news. Assigning one to reasoning and the other to storage is a modern HIVE reinterpretation, not a recovered claim about their original roles. 3.3 The execution recipe is the main bridge A useful recipe records: - Task class and applicability conditions. - Capabilities and exact versions used. - Dependencies, parallel branches, and communication contracts. - Memory scopes and required inputs. - Resource limits and observed costs. - Verifier results, failures, and known limitations. - Conditions that invalidate the recipe. Retrieve a recipe as a candidate. Recheck current capabilities and task conditions before running it. A successful answer alone does not establish that the same combination generalizes. 4. Odysseus and the 25-project inventory 4.1 What to extract from Odysseus The official Odysseus repository describes a self-hosted workspace for agents, research, documents, communications, notes, and local-model workflows. The research identified useful mechanisms within that broader product. The official skill-audit design documents these mechanisms: 1. Compare skill and no-skill runs on the same task. 2. Grade results and permit bounded worker revisions. 3. Optionally use a distinct teacher to rewrite the skill, then retry with the worker. 4. Apply separate publication rules, including usefulness and duplicate checks. HIVE proposal: adopt the comparison pattern, then add task-specific checkers and held-out evaluation. A grader’s confidence field is not a calibrated probability of correctness. An audit pass is evidence for a particular version under particular conditions. The recovered discussion also emphasized separate records for raw experience, memory candidates, and reusable skills. Its runtime lessons concerned ownership, execution contracts, cancellation, recovery, and verification of effects. The official migration account corroborates those runtime concerns. 4.2 Odysseus and Ajax are separate The official Ajax page describes Ajax as a Qwen 3.5 9B fine-tune intended for Odysseus. On 20 November 2026 it still stated that release would occur when ready. Dependency decision: study the available Odysseus implementation now. Keep Ajax as a candidate whose actual release and local suitability must be checked before adoption. 4.3 The recovered 25-project catalog The names and links below reconstruct the original comparison inventory from R2. The final column is a proposed inspection question, not a recovered performance ranking or a commitment to install every project. These projects occupy different layers of a system. Project and source What the coder should inspect for HIVE ---:------ 1 OpenClaw Persistent assistant operation, tool boundaries, and channels into existing workflows. 2 Hermes Agent How experience becomes reusable procedural knowledge and compact memory. 3 Agent Zero Delegation, execution context, and containment of subordinate work. 4 Goose Extensible tool interfaces and practical local execution. 5 Open Interpreter Interfaces between model reasoning and executable computer operations. 6 OpenHands Coding-agent workspaces, execution traces, and feedback from actual code results. 7 LifeOS Persistent personal goals, context organization, and reusable operating procedures. 8 Open WebUI Operator interfaces and model/tool integration boundaries. 9 LibreChat Provider abstraction, conversations, and agent-facing interfaces. 10 AnythingLLM Workspace knowledge retrieval and document-to-agent integration. 11 LobeHub Specialist configuration, user interaction, and context organization. 12 Khoj Connection between existing notes, including Obsidian, and assistant retrieval. 13 Jan Local-model usability and runtime integration. 14 GPT4All Local inference and document-assisted workflows as a baseline. 15 Dify Explicit workflows, knowledge integration, and observable execution steps. 16 Flowise Visual workflow representation and handoff design; retain as a historical reference. 17 Langflow Packaging workflow combinations into reusable components or tools. 18 LangGraph Durable execution state, checkpoints, and recovery of failed branches. 19 Microsoft Agent Framework Structured orchestration, subsystem contracts, and checkpoint boundaries. 20 CrewAI Role-based coordination as one measurable topology baseline. 21 MagenticLite Controller-plus-specialist division, especially orchestration and browser work. 22 Letta / Letta Code Persistent memory, conversation retrieval, and consolidation through sleeptime. 23 Graphiti Temporal relationships, source lineage, and changes in recorded knowledge. 24 Mem0 Selective memory extraction, updates, retrieval, and scope. 25 Cognee Narrow extraction and structuring stages for the knowledge pipeline. Specific source checks affecting selection: - Flowise was archived on 13 August 2026. Its historical design remains inspectable; a new dependency needs a separate maintenance decision. - The microsoft/magentic-ui repository currently identifies itself as MagenticLite. Preserve this name-to-repository mapping. - Repository existence does not establish installation, local compatibility, benchmark quality, or suitability for HIVE. Priority mechanisms from the recovered discussion: Odysseus skill auditing; MagenticLite’s controller/specialist split; Hermes procedures; Letta consolidation; Graphiti provenance; Khoj’s note bridge; LangGraph or Microsoft Agent Framework for durable coordination; Cognee for extraction. Select the smallest combination that implements a measured capability. Record interfaces, revisions, and licensing conditions before incorporating code. 5. Fictional hive minds as architecture stress tests 5.1 Preserve the four structural categories The research distinguished the following categories. Their software translations remain hypotheses. Fictional category Software question ------ One distributed person across bodies Which shared state and continuity rules define one logical agent across multiple processes? Individuals sharing thoughts What should independent agents share while preserving local memory, uncertainty, and autonomy? Swarm computation Which tasks can local rules and limited messages solve without global deliberation? A ruler controlling a population Where does central authority simplify coordination, and where does it create a bottleneck or failure point? This distinction prevents the word “hive” from hiding different architectures. Colony-level computation does not by itself establish shared consciousness. 5.2 Recovered examples and proposed tests Example recovered in R3 Lesson in the retrieved discussion Proposed experiment --------- Vernor Vinge’s Tines Proximity and communication affect effective cognition. Restrict bandwidth, add delay, remove members, and measure capability under changed connectivity. Ann Leckie’s distributed AIs Shared infrastructure can coexist with conflicting selves. Fork state, allow divergence, and test identity, ownership, and reconciliation. Brandon Sanderson’s Sleepless Division can alter identity and complicate coordination. Split a group, assign different experiences, then test reconstruction or explicitly separate continuation. Formics Strong coordination can coexist with serious collective mistakes. Give several specialists the same false premise and measure whether independent evidence corrects it. Ant-kinden Collective coordination does not guarantee strategic success. Compare coordination efficiency with externally measured task success. Patternists A powerful collective can still fail at its aims. Separate authority, agreement, and outcome quality in the evaluation record. These are reasons to design experiments. They supply no numerical prediction of HIVE performance. 5.3 Preserve all three evaluation axes Original axis Meaning to retain HIVE measurement alongside it --------- Internal-rule consistency Does the fictional system follow its own established mechanisms? Do runtime actions follow declared contracts and state rules? Collective-intelligence value How useful is the example for understanding a collective? Does the proposed mechanism offer a testable design insight? Competence at its aims Does the collective achieve identifiable goals? Task success, quality, recovery, latency, and resource use. Do not combine the axes into one “best hive” score without an explicit weighting decision. Where a planetary consciousness has no clear strategic goal, mark competence not assessable under this criterion. Import gap: keep the missing 15 names and original ratings as unresolved source fields. The earlier 21-system comparison must be recovered before reproducing its complete table. 6. Proposed architecture and module boundaries 6.1 One execution loop and one improvement loop mermaid flowchart TD T["Task and constraints"] -- C["Controller and registry"] C -- G["Selected models and tools"] M["Scoped memory"] -- G G -- V["Evidence and verification"] V --sufficient O["Result"] V --recoverable failure R["Bounded recovery"] R -- C V --unrecoverable F["Failure report and saved state"] R --budget exhausted F F -- E G -- E["Execution record"] V -- E E -- L["Consolidation and candidates"] L -- Q["Evaluation against baseline"] Q --passes gates P["Versioned promotion"] Q --fails or inconclusive A["Retained experiment"] P -- C P -- M Typed contracts govern the connections. Watchdogs observe execution independently of the controller’s conversational attention. 6.2 Module responsibilities Module Responsibility Boundary --------- Capability registry Describe tools, models, adapters, workflows, versions, inputs, outputs, costs, and readiness. Capability claims require a readiness test; a registry entry alone proves nothing. Task controller Characterize work, select a recipe or candidate composition, and allocate budget. Selection policy is replaceable and evaluated separately from workers. Execution kernel Schedule dependencies, issue leases, record events, cancel, retry, and resume. Essential lifecycle bookkeeping should remain available when a model stalls. Specialist adapters Expose local models, external models, deterministic tools, and procedures through contracts. Preserve distinctions among a model, an adapter, a prompt role, and a tool. Translators Convert representations and validate meaning-bearing fields. Unknown or incompatible fields remain explicit. Memory service Store and retrieve scoped episodic, semantic, and procedural records. Visibility and promotion rules determine what can cross compartments. Evidence and verification service Check claims, artifacts, and observed effects against task criteria. Agreement among models is not sufficient verification. Local supervisors Detect stalls and recurring local failures; apply bounded known repairs. Their authority and budget are explicit. Learning workbench Produce candidate memory, skill, routing, topology, code, or parameter changes. Experimental artifacts remain distinguishable from active versions. Release registry Track compatible versions, promotions, and rollback targets. Historical runs retain their original attribution after upgrades. 6.3 Four graphs with different meanings Retain the earlier framework’s distinction: Graph Represents Authoritative record --------- Research Topics, claims, sources, metaphors, experiments, disagreements. Markdown notes and typed links. Code Modules, symbols, imports, and dependencies. Source at a pinned revision; Graphify is a derived index. Execution Runtime capabilities, ordering, messages, and budgets. Versioned recipes plus event records. Neural Layers, learned parameters, experts, adapters, and checkpoints. Exact model manifests. A link in the research graph can explain an execution decision; it does not itself modify a model. 7. Data contracts and learning lifecycle 7.1 Minimum records Field names below are proposed starting contracts, not existing APIs. Record Essential fields ------ Task task_id, goal, inputs, constraints, budget, deadline, success_checks, owner Capability capability_id, kind, version, runtime, input_schema, output_schema, memory_scope, permissions, readiness, cost_profile Message message_id, task_id, correlation_id, sender_instance, recipient, channel, schema_version, payload_ref, provenance, expiry, idempotency_key Claim claim_id, content, scope, evidence_refs, status, uncertainty_basis, contradicts, observed_at, valid_at Execution recipe recipe_id, version, applicability, graph, capability_versions, translator_versions, budgets, validation_refs, invalidation_conditions Run run_id, task_id, recipe_version, input_refs, events, outputs, resource_usage, verifier_results, failures Memory memory_id, type, scope, source_refs, created_at, validity, retention_rule, status, supersedes Identity logical_id, instance_id, parent_id, model_version, memory_version, fork_point, merge_record Change candidate change_id, kind, parent_version, hypothesis, affected_components, training_or_generation_data, evaluation_refs, status, rollback_target Experiment experiment_id, baseline, candidate, dataset_version, budget, metrics, repetitions, results, limitations, decision Decision decision_id, alternatives, evidence_for, evidence_against, owner, selected_option, provisional, reopening_conditions 7.2 Communication channels Preserve the existing four-channel direction, with distinct authority: Channel Payload Required handling --------- Control Allocation, lifecycle, cancellation, permissions. Authenticate the sender’s authority; validate target and scope. Task Work requests, dependencies, progress, outputs. Track ownership, deadlines, state transitions, and duplicate delivery. Evidence Observations, sources, test results, uncertainty. Preserve provenance and distinguish observation from inference. Teaching Examples, corrections, procedures, proposed updates. Admit as candidates; promotion follows evaluation. Different local representations do not require a universal new language at the outset. Compare typed exchanges, natural-language exchanges, and hybrids under equal budgets. Typed messages improve inspectability but do not automatically guarantee semantic accuracy. For calls with external effects, keep a stable operation identity across retries and use provider-supported idempotency where available. After a timeout or crash with uncertain completion, record outcome_unknown and reconcile the actual effect before retrying. An execution log alone cannot guarantee exactly-once execution. If the effect cannot be checked and a retry could duplicate it, retain the unresolved state instead of blindly replaying the call. 7.3 Keep learning mechanisms separately measurable Mechanism What changes Required evidence --------- Experience accumulation Archived observations and actions. Complete, attributable records. Memory consolidation Retrieval entries, summaries, retention, and scope. Retrieval quality, retained knowledge, and contamination checks. Skill learning Reusable procedures or instructions. Skill/no-skill comparison plus held-out tasks. Routing adaptation Which capability is selected and when. Quality and cost against a fixed selector. Topology adaptation Grouping, communication, and supervision. Equal-budget comparison of structures and failure behavior. Parameter learning Weights, adapters, heads, or model checkpoints. Training lineage, held-out performance, retention, and rollback. Software improvement Code, tools, and integration behavior. Reproducible task improvement and relevant regression checks. Sleep-inspired work can contain replay, consolidation, rehearsal, compression, or parameter updates. Evaluate each mechanism and combination explicitly. A replay result alone does not settle whether the other mechanisms help. 7.4 Candidate lifecycle 1. Capture a trace, correction, or recurring failure. 2. State a hypothesis and identify the baseline version. 3. Generate a bounded candidate change. 4. Evaluate on development cases without exposing reserved evaluation answers. 5. Test held-out cases and affected existing capabilities. 6. Record outcome quality, costs, failures, and uncertainty. 7. Promote only when the predeclared gates pass. 8. Keep the previous version available and record what rollback can restore. A rejected or inconclusive candidate remains part of the research record. Rollback restores software or configuration state; real-world effects need their own recorded recovery or compensation. 8. Build sequence and acceptance checks 8.1 Work packages These packages define observable deliverables rather than an unsupported calendar estimate. Package Work Acceptance --------- WP0 — Map the existing build Inspect the repository, vault, inventory, runtimes, and actual hardware budgets. Classify components as working, installed but untested, source-only, or unavailable. A delta map identifies reusable components, missing interfaces, and conflicting prior decisions. WP1 — Define contracts and a baseline Implement registry, task/message schemas, event records, and a single-model-plus-tools baseline. A representative task produces an artifact, a verification result, and an attributable run record. WP2 — Add bounded coordination Connect a small specialist group, typed translators, scoped memory, and a watchdog. Keep worker count configurable. The same task completes; a stalled worker is detected and recovered or explicitly stopped within budget. WP3 — Reuse successful configurations Extract and retrieve execution recipes with applicability and version checks. A compatible task can reuse a recipe; an incompatible version or missing capability triggers a recorded rejection or adaptation. WP4 — Add consolidation and skill auditing Produce memory/skill candidates and compare them against the baseline. A candidate is evaluated on held-out work; regressions block promotion; rollback remains executable. WP5 — Test alternative organizations Compare centralized, hierarchical, peer, and dynamically grouped execution. Inject partition and disagreement failures. Results report quality, cost, delay, fault propagation, and uncertainty for each tested configuration. WP6 — Exercise real workflows Apply the stable slice to the three existing application directions. Each pilot produces useful output and measured task-specific results. WP7 — Extend learned specialization Test adapters, weight changes, or other specialist learning as explicit experiments. Improvement and retention are measured separately from routing or memory changes. WP0–WP2 are the first executable slice. A small initial group establishes working interfaces and baselines; it does not set a permanent ceiling on HIVE’s population. 8.2 Meaningful acceptance scenarios Test Setup Passing observation --------- Translation Two specialists use different units or schemas; include an unmappable field. Valid conversions preserve meaning; unsupported fields trigger an explicit incompatibility. Memory contamination Supply a false claim inside one specialist’s unverified memory. It remains scoped and does not silently become shared validated knowledge. Collective error Several specialists share a misleading premise; another has corrective evidence. The corrective branch survives and the decision records how its evidence was evaluated. Stall recovery Stop a worker or tool while a task is active. A watchdog detects the condition, bounds retries, and records recovery or failure. Partition and reconciliation Disconnect groups, create conflicting updates, then reconnect. Both histories survive; conflicts are visible; idempotent effects are not duplicated and ambiguous effects are reconciled before replay. Repair regression A candidate fixes one case but breaks another established capability. Promotion is blocked and the previous version remains usable. Replacement continuity Replace a model or translator after successful runs. Past outputs retain original version attribution; affected recipes are revalidated. Recipe generalization Test a saved configuration on unseen tasks and changed conditions. Results distinguish genuine transfer from reuse that fails applicability checks. 8.3 Measurements and comparison discipline Compare a deterministic tool route where applicable, one model with tools, a fixed specialist configuration, and adaptive configurations. Measurement Report ------ Task quality Task-specific success, correctness, completeness, and artifact validity. Responsiveness Median and p95 end-to-end latency; time to first useful output where relevant. Resources Wall time, VRAM/RAM use, model residency, active workers, tokens, and tool calls. Coordination cost Message volume, translation time, synchronization delay, and retries. Recovery Detection time, recovery time, unfinished tasks, and duplicated effects. Learning Held-out improvement, regression rate, retention, contamination, and transfer. Use the same task set and resource budget when attributing gains to architecture. Report best-effort performance separately. Repeat stochastic runs and report sample counts and variation; preserve inconclusive outcomes. Application-specific checks: - Video production: artifact correctness, revision burden, completion time, and continuity of project memory. - Live calls and supervisor streaming: response delay, interruption handling, stalls, and resource interference with the live production stack. - Horror-haunt game: event response, persistent world/character state, conflicting events, and recovery after interruptions. 9. Decisions that remain open Decision Alternatives to retain Experiment that should guide the choice --------- Specialist implementation Independent models; shared backbone with adapters; internal experts; deterministic tools; hybrids. Equal-budget quality, residency cost, transfer, and interference. Coordination Central selector; hierarchy; peer groups; dynamic communities. Completion quality, communication cost, failure containment, and partition behavior. Shared knowledge Broad shared memory; scoped stores; explicit promotion between compartments. Retrieval benefit, leakage, contradiction handling, and contamination. Communication Natural language; typed records; hybrids; later learned representations. Semantic errors, translation overhead, auditability, and task success. Verification Deterministic checks; task-specific tools; model graders; human review for unresolved cases. Error detection and correlated failure on a representative evaluation set. Consolidation Continuous updates; scheduled offline work; event-triggered consolidation. Retention, interference with live tasks, resource use, and improvement. Learning target Procedures, routing, topology, memory, parameters, or combinations. Ablations isolating which change produced the result. Framework reuse Existing local components; one external runtime; selective adapters. Integration effort, recovery behavior, dependency burden, and measurable benefit. Every decision record needs evidence for and against, a provisional choice, a test, and reopening conditions. Preserve discarded candidates with the reason they were set aside. 10. Research vault integration 10.1 Topic-first layout Use these as logical note groups within the existing vault; adapt names to its current structure. Group Contents ------ HIVE overview Mission, architecture map, present status, and this handoff. Topics Specialist organization, communication, memory, learning, governance, verification, recovery. Sources Conversation summaries, inspected repositories, papers, books, and exact source locations when available. Metaphors Original meaning, HIVE interpretation, limits, and linked experiment. Decisions Alternatives, evidence, provisional defaults, and reopening conditions. Experiments Hypothesis, baseline, candidate, data, budgets, metrics, results, and failure cases. Implementation Contracts, modules, code references, capability readiness, and integration notes. History Previous attempts, negative results, superseded proposals, and links explaining each change. Keep the earlier six research lanes for each topic: direct, competing, boundary, adjacent, implementation, and history. Use meaningful links such as supports, contradicts, implements, tests, derived-from, and supersedes. Preserve original material when a conclusion changes. 10.2 Example traceable chain A K-lines note links to the execution recipe hypothesis. That hypothesis links to the recipe schema and implementation. Those link to a held-out reuse experiment. The result links to the adoption or rejection decision. This makes it possible to move from an inspiring idea to code and back to the evidence for keeping it. 10.3 Import record template yaml id: HIVE-RESEARCH-EXAMPLE title: Successful specialist combinations evidence_class: proposed_implementation derived_from: - R1 - R2 topic: execution_recipes claim: Retrieving validated recipes may reduce repeated planning cost. alternatives: - plan_each_task_from_scratch - fixed_workflow experiment: EXP-RECIPE-REUSE status: untested supersedes: [] reopen_when: - required_capability_changes - held_out_quality_regresses The identifiers above illustrate the schema; they do not refer to existing completed experiments. 11. Direct instructions to the coder Start with the current HIVE repository and research vault. Read existing local instructions and produce a delta map before restructuring components. Implement the smallest complete path that accepts a task, chooses capabilities, exchanges typed messages, records evidence, verifies an output, and detects a stalled dependency. Establish the single-model-plus-tools baseline in the same harness. Then add versioned execution recipes and one bounded learning mechanism. Compare the learned candidate with its baseline on reserved tasks. Retain failed experiments and support rollback before expanding the adaptive behavior. Maintain these distinctions throughout: - A source observation, a model inference, and a verified result. - A saved memory, a learned procedure, a changed routing policy, and changed model weights. - A logical specialist, a running worker, and a resident model. - A research analogy, an implementation proposal, and a measured capability. - A replay of recorded events, a rerun with stochastic models, and an exactly reproducible deterministic computation. Required return package - [ ] Reuse/missing-component map and local readiness report. - [ ] Architecture diagram and initial decision records. - [ ] Versioned task, message, capability, memory, recipe, and run contracts. - [ ] Working baseline and first specialist configuration. - [ ] Run commands, pinned dependencies, and reproducible task inputs. - [ ] Relevant translation, scope, failure, and regression checks. - [ ] Measured quality, resource use, latency, and recovery results. - [ ] One evaluated learning candidate, including an honest failed or inconclusive result if it does not improve. - [ ] Linked research notes and unresolved source gaps. - [ ] Exact next experiment justified by the observed result. 12. Sources and recovery limits R1. Philosophy and mythology Conversation: “Research Philosophy and Mythology,” 20 November 2026. User request: research philosophy, mental frameworks, and mythology for useful parallels and metaphors for HIVE. Recovered: the named frameworks and metaphors in Section 3, including qualifications about pluralism, meaningful dissent, and Odin’s ravens. Limits: full transcript, complete original bibliography, and conversation permalink were not returned. The software translations in this packet are proposals. Do not cite them as empirical validation of the philosophical claims. R2. Odysseus and related projects Conversation: “Analyze Odysseus Projects,” 20 November 2026. User request: examine what HIVE can learn from PewDiePie’s Odysseus project and identify 25 similar projects. Recovered: all 25 inventory names and repository links; skill auditing; distinct archive, memory, and procedural layers; execution/recovery contracts; controller/specialist patterns. Primary sources checked for the central claims: - Odysseus repository and README. - Odysseus skill evaluation and audit architecture. - Odysseus pre-Ajax migration account. - Official Ajax status and description. - Flowise repository and archive notice. - MagenticLite repository identity. The 25-project table contains the remaining source links. Source checks establish identity and the specific documented behaviors; no local HIVE performance comparison was run. R3. Fictional hive minds Conversation: “Research Hive Minds,” 20 November 2026. User request: examine fantasy and science-fiction hive minds, their operation and structure, and rate consistency, value, and competence. Recovered: four structural categories; the three distinct axes; six examples; communication, identity, division, and collective-error lessons. Limits: the complete 21-system list, original numerical scores, full literary citations, and conversation permalink remain unavailable. No missing rankings were invented. R4. Existing HIVE foundation These earlier artifacts provide continuity; they are not counted among the three research conversations: - HIVE_Framework_and_Research_Plan.md — opening framework sections reviewed for commitments, graph separation, components, and research structure. - HIVE_Research_Synthesis_Coder_Handoff_v0.3.md — previous short synthesis reviewed in full. This revision expands the philosophical and mythological inventory, restores all 25 project links, and makes the coder requirements and tests explicit. It also replaces the earlier blanket expectation of deterministic replay with a distinction between event replay, stochastic reruns, and deterministic computations.

title: Adaptive organization and self-learning
text: HIVE — Research Update: Adaptive Organization and Self-Learning Database update purpose: Add the recent organizational findings and decisions to the HIVE knowledge base. This is a research and design handoff, not a claim that the proposed architecture has been built or proven. Keep conflicting approaches as separate, linkable candidates. Prioritize the self-learning system, because successful compounding learning could improve other HIVE capabilities. 0. Change log — what is new ID Finding / change Classification Database action ------------ NEW-01 Organization itself is a learnable component. Topology, routing, communication, verification, group membership, and memory access can be treated as adjustable variables. Research-derived design hypothesis Add to core architecture thesis. NEW-02 Do not choose one side of most organizational tensions. Use both where complementary; switch or blend according to task conditions. User-selected design direction Promote to provisional architectural requirement. NEW-03 Distinguish composition, reliability, current-task adaptation, persistent learning, and integrated individuality. Conceptual clarification Create separate concepts and benchmarks. NEW-04 Separate specialist learning from organizational learning. Improvement can occur without changing any model weights. Architecture principle; not yet a HIVE measurement Create independent update and evaluation loops. NEW-05 Communication and coordination have costs. More agents, debate, and shared context can reduce performance. Research-supported boundary condition Require matched-budget baselines and ablation tests. NEW-06 Memory is not learning. Outcomes must change future behavior and survive independent testing to count as learned improvement. Conceptual + engineering principle Separate memory, skills, routing, weights, and topology updates. NEW-07 Treat the governing/rating formulas as a family, selected by task and framework—not a universal score. User research priority + proposed design Create formula registry, contexts, constraints, and experiments. NEW-08 Preserve independent disagreement, evidence provenance, fault isolation, rollback, and autonomy within bounds. Convergent engineering principle Add architectural invariants and failure tests. NEW-09 Biological, spiritual, philosophical, and fictional hive examples suggest hypotheses but do not demonstrate machine consciousness, universal swarm superiority, or specific AI mechanisms. Evidence boundary Store analogy and empirical evidence separately. NEW-10 Prefer selectively permeable specialist boundaries: isolation by process/store/permissions/protocol, with typed translators at boundaries; language choice alone does not prevent contamination. Prior HIVE design inference Add information-flow security research item. Evidence legend - [SOURCE] Explicit in the uploaded research files or established work cited in those files. - [SYNTHESIS] Reasoned integration of the sources; not necessarily independently experimentally confirmed. - [DECISION] Direction expressly chosen in recent HIVE discussions; not proof of efficacy. - [HYPOTHESIS] Proposed implementation or expected benefit requiring tests. - [OPEN] Unresolved empirical or architectural question. - [ANALOGY] Biological, spiritual, sociological, or fictional parallel, not a validated AI mechanism. - [PREVIOUS-WORK] Recovered from earlier HIVE discussion; not retested for this packet. --- 1. Core thesis and the five different outcomes Core thesis [SYNTHESIS]: HIVE is a modular, persistent, self-improving cognitive organization in which the relationships among imperfect specialists are themselves designed, observed, tested, and eventually adapted. The framework can contribute capability independently of changes to specialist weights. Outcome Meaning What would demonstrate it What it does not establish ------------ Compositional capability Specialists jointly complete a task no single specialist covers end-to-end. End-to-end success with demonstrated complementary contributions. That the group learns or is more accurate on all tasks. Collective reliability Diverse error paths, verification, and recovery increase successful completion. Higher held-out task success, with matched cost/compute. Consciousness or novelty of intelligence. Adaptive coordination The group changes its operating mode in response to a task, failure, or available compute. Observable, beneficial selection of routing/topology/checking policy. Persistent improvement across later tasks. Persistent learning The organization retains an update that improves subsequent unfamiliar tasks. Future held-out gain, transferable learning, bounded forgetting, reproducibility. Any specific change to neural weights. Integrated individuality Components form an unusually tightly dependent collective; in biology this has specific evolutionary criteria. Would require its own carefully defined technical test. Subjective awareness or an AI “soul.” Important distinction: Increased task success under collaboration is not automatically evidence of a new unified mind. The engineering goal is measurable cognitive capability and learning; consciousness remains a separate philosophical and scientific question. --- 2. Twelve consolidated organizational principles This unifies the five computational clusters and nine biological/spiritual themes with the preceding HIVE analysis. The list is a working taxonomy, not twelve proven laws jointly necessary for every system. Key Principle Mechanism and HIVE translation Risks / limits ------------ ORG-01 Dependency-aware decomposition Divide tasks where coupling is low; preserve interdependent constraints and handoff meaning. Too many handoffs; missing global constraints. ORG-02 Complementary diversity Different capabilities, tools, inputs, and error patterns—not merely more copies of one model. Correlated failures; costly redundancy. ORG-03 Competence-aware routing Choose workers by demonstrated task-conditioned success, cost, latency, and uncertainty. Miscalibration; controller bottleneck. ORG-04 Typed selective communication Explicit claims, evidence, sources, semantics, validity windows, and receivers. Semantic contamination; message floods. ORG-05 Independent verification Separate generating candidates from executable checks, independent evidence, and environmental results. Shared verifier blind spots; excessive rejection. ORG-06 Epistemic memory Store hypothesis, evidence, accepted result, failed experiment, and reusable skill distinctly. False information promoted to trusted memory. ORG-07 Fault containment Timeouts, least privilege, isolation, rollback, circuit breakers, graceful fallback. Cascading failures; lost recovery state. ORG-08 Flexible topology Allow central, distributed, nested, and hybrid coordination according to dependencies. Over-orchestration or chaotic local interactions. ORG-09 Exploration and selection Maintain competing solutions; select using tests and graded evidence. Premature consensus; lock-in; reward hacking. ORG-10 System-level objectives and budgets Allocate compute, memory, bandwidth, and authority by collective outcomes. Local optimization harming overall performance. ORG-11 Lifecycle and renewal Reuse, retrain, compress, prune, replace, or revive elements after evaluation. Instability, regressions, catastrophic forgetting. ORG-12 Shared operational purpose with dissent Clear task goals, policies, and allowed actions; protect independent criticism. Groupthink and suppressing legitimate alternatives. Cross-domain notes [ANALOGY]: Immune repertoires suggest diversity, bee scouts suggest competing exploration with a quorum, multicellularity suggests differentiated roles and conflict management, and social/spiritual traditions suggest questions of purpose and mutual obligation. These are sources of design questions, not proof that their literal biological or theological mechanisms transfer to software. --- 3. Major decision: adaptive organizational duality Decision DEC-ORG-BOTH-001 [DECISION]: Most disagreements should be treated as potentially complementary operating modes. HIVE must not hard-code centralized versus decentralized, competition versus cooperation, or shared versus isolated state as mutually exclusive universal choices. Preserve all useful candidates and test when to operate them simultaneously, switch between them, or blend them. 3.1 Three distinct meanings of “use both” 1. Simultaneous combination: Different mechanisms run concurrently because they do different jobs (e.g., central policy constraints alongside autonomous local workers). 2. Contextual switching: One mode replaces another when task properties or costs change (e.g., independent search for parallel problems, tighter control for interdependent execution). 3. Adaptive blending: The controller continuously varies strength, budget, membership, and information flow across modes (e.g., percentage of compute used for exploration versus verification). Constraint: “Use both” does not mean activate all mechanisms all the time. Each must justify its cost, interference, safety implications, and effect on whole-system performance. 3.2 Discrepancy-to-combination decision table Duality Combined policy candidate Potential selection signals Failure conditions to measure ------------ Centralized ↔ decentralized Central policy/constraint management; autonomous local execution and recruitment. Coupling, deadlines, criticality, failure rates, communication load. Bottlenecks; unsupervised drift. Cooperation ↔ competition Shared final objective; independent candidate-generation and competing proposals. Uncertainty, alternative count, verification quality. Conformity; adversarial waste. Consensus ↔ disagreement Preserve dissent during exploration; commit after evidence-based choice or explicit deadline/quorum. Verifiability, irreversibility, time budget. Majority confidently wrong; paralysis. Specialization ↔ redundancy Primary narrow specialists plus overlapping fallback/checker coverage. Failure severity, costs, availability, correlated error. Brittle dependency; unnecessary copies. Shared ↔ isolated memory Shared evidence registry/index; protected local scratchpads, procedures, and parameter state. Sensitivity, relevance, source trust, recency, access needs. Contamination, leakage, loss of context. Dependence ↔ independence Reusable standalone modules form temporary tightly coupled teams where needed. Task dependency graph, interface maturity, recovery cost. Irreversible coupling; integration overhead. Exploration ↔ exploitation Stable production policy plus bounded experiment lanes. Novelty, expected information gain, remaining budget, error tolerance. Stagnation; experimental instability. Autonomy ↔ policing Local discretion constrained by contracts, monitors, and reversible interventions. Risk level, observed reliability, novelty, rule violations. Overcontrol; unchecked errors. Stability ↔ evolution Tested baseline serves tasks while candidate improvements undergo replay/regression tests. Held-out gains, forgetting, cost and recovery. Catastrophic regressions; frozen design. Small ↔ large teams Dynamic staffing and compute allocation; recruit additional workers only when marginal value is positive. Subtask independence, expected gains, latency and budget. Coordination cost exceeds added capability. Shared representations ↔ specialist representations Typed common contracts at the boundary; local embeddings/modalities with explicit translators. Fidelity of translation, alignment need, contamination risk. Translation loss; interoperability cost. Online ↔ offline learning Fast response-time correction and slower batch consolidation, evaluation, retraining, or pruning. Task urgency, replay availability, change risk. Unchecked self-edits; stale information. 3.3 Governing principle Unity without uniformity: HIVE needs sufficient shared constraints to act coherently, and sufficient differentiated independence to discover mistakes, remain replaceable, and continue learning. Unresolved [OPEN]: The optimal switch/blend policy and its cost are not established. An adaptive hybrid is a candidate, not a demonstrated winner over a simpler controller. --- 4. What should be learnable — independent layers The initial priority is to improve learning speed, retention, transfer, and reliable promotion of improvements. Keep at least six different update targets separate: Layer Adjustable variables (“dials”) How improvement would appear --------- L1 External / episodic memory Retention, retrieval, relevance, provenance, confidence evidence Better recall/use of prior evidence without escalating stale errors. L2 Procedural skills Tool sequences, reusable workflows, preconditions, success checks Faster, cheaper, more reliable completion of repeatable tasks. L3 Routing and resource policy Specialist selection, effort, parallelism, escalation threshold Better outcomes per resource and less avoidable delay. L4 Specialist parameters Fine-tuning, adapters, distillation, selective pruning Improved measured specialist task performance. L5 Organizational topology Team membership, control structure, verification depth, interaction graph Better collective performance with the same or comparable components. L6 Communication and representation Protocol, schema, bandwidth, translators, isolation, representation choice Less handoff loss and contamination at useful coordination cost. Other variables include when to verify, when to abstain, when to reuse a cached result, when to combine specialists, and when to deactivate or replace a component. Non-equivalences to preserve: - Memory accumulation ≠ procedural learning ≠ weight updates ≠ organizational policy learning. - A different programming language (Rust, Python, C++, JavaScript, etc.) ≠ automatic isolation; process, permission, storage, schema, and validation boundaries matter. - Quantization ≠ pruning ≠ distillation ≠ fine-tuning ≠ adapter switching. Each trades capability, cost, and reversibility differently. - Different model identities ≠ uncorrelated errors. Measure correlation empirically. 4.1 Dual learning loops mermaid flowchart TD A[Task and observations] -- B[Decompose and select operating modes] B -- C[Recruit specialists and tools] C -- D[Local compute and selective exchange] D -- E[Independent tests and evidence] E -- F{Pass constraints?} F --No G[Revise / isolate / escalate / abstain] G -- B F --Yes H[Commit result and provenance] H -- I[Experience log and graded memory] I -- J[Learning workbench: propose one bounded change] J -- K[Replay + held-out + regression evaluation] K -- L{Promotion governor passes?} L --No M[Reject, archive evidence, keep baseline] L --Yes N[Promote versioned policy, skill, or model] N -- B Fast/task loop: Observe → decompose → recruit → work → verify → recover/commit. Slow/improvement loop: Attribute outcome → propose bounded update → evaluate against unchanged serving baseline → promote or roll back → record conditions and evidence. [HYPOTHESIS] The slow loop can improve the group while weights remain frozen, by changing topology, routing, coordination, verification, or memory policies. This must be tested against static and simpler baselines. 4.2 Why self-learning comes first Compounding learning requires more than recalling successful past solutions. A stronger measurable criterion is future unfamiliar tasks becoming learnable with fewer examples, less compute, or fewer trials without unacceptable forgetting. Track that separately from routine-task acceleration through caching or skill reuse. Previous HIVE research considered periodic consolidation/replay (“sleep-like” cycles). One earlier replay comparison, not a complete HIVE sleep system, reported interleaved replay 74.47%, blocked replay 62.64%, and current-only 54.31% under that study's evaluation. Preserve those numbers with their original context; do not relabel them as HIVE benchmark results, proof of dreaming, or proof of beneficial autonomous weight changes. [PREVIOUS-WORK] --- 5. Governing formulas and rating layers (self-learning priority) Decision / research direction [DECISION]: No single formula should be assumed optimal across every procedure framework. Build a formula registry: each candidate specifies the decision it governs, inputs, assumptions, constraints, evidence, calibration method, and benchmark. Keep local scores distinct from the global objective. 5.1 Existing mathematical families worth testing Formula family Representative expression Suitable role Important limitation ------------ Bayesian update P(HD) = P(DH) P(H) / P(D) Revise belief using evidence. Requires meaningful hypotheses, likelihoods and priors. Expected information gain EIG(e) = H(ΘD) − E_y[H(ΘD,e,y)] Choose informative experiments/observations. Information gain alone may not improve task utility. Learning progress LP_t = S_t − S_(t−k) Detect whether skills are improving on a stable metric. Can chase noise or easy-to-game tests. Value of computation VOC(c) = E_z[max_a U(aD,z_c)] − max_a U(aD) − C(c) Decide whether another agent call/check/search is worth its cost. Utility and future evidence must be estimated. Upper confidence bound / bandits UCB_i = r̄_i + c √(ln(t)/n_i) Explore potentially good specialists/strategies while exploiting known ones. Standard assumptions may fail for changing tasks and correlated arms. Temporal-difference error δ_t = r_t + γ max_a Q(s_(t+1),a) − Q(s_t,a_t) Learn sequential action/routing policies. Reward design and nonstationarity can mislead. Prioritized replay, EWC, information bottleneck See primary work / prior formula research Retention, consolidation, forgetting constraints, compression. No universal objective or proven HIVE integration yet. Difference rewards / credit assignment Compare observed group outcome to a counterfactual baseline. Estimate which specialist and organizational change contributed. Counterfactual baselines may be costly or biased. Meta-learning, constrained policy improvement Family of task-dependent methods Improve learning-to-learn and promote safe bounded updates. Complex testing and stability requirements. The equations in this subsection are standard representative forms recovered from the recent governing-formulas discussion; they have not been tested within HIVE. Notation must be defined and calibrated for each implementation. 5.2 Proposed HIVE formulas — unvalidated design candidates Expected Learning Value (candidate) \[ V(e\mid x)=\mathbb{E}[\Delta J_{\mathrm{future}}\mid e,x]-\lambda_C C(e)-\lambda_F F(e)-\lambda_R R(e) \] - e: proposed experiment or learning intervention; x: current state/context. - ΔJ_future: expected improvement on future task performance, not only present-task success. - C: compute/time/energy cost; F: expected forgetting/interference; R: risk of regression/unsafe change. - λ: context-dependent trade-off weights; not empirically fitted yet. - Use a vector of raw metrics and explicit hard constraints alongside any aggregate score to prevent a high score from disguising a catastrophic regression. Promotion governor (candidate) \[ \operatorname{Promote}(u)=\mathbf{1}\!\left[\mathrm{LCB}(\Delta J_u)\delta\ \land\ \mathrm{RegressionGates}(u)=\mathrm{pass}\right] \] - u: proposed update; LCB: defensible lower confidence bound of measured gain on held-out evaluation; δ: required benefit margin. - Regression gates should cover failure rate, forgetting, resource budgets, reproducibility, and rollback readiness. - This is a proposal, not a validated probability model or automatic authority to deploy changes. 5.3 Candidate measurement dashboard Metric Question answered ------ Held-out task success Is the whole system more capable? Reliability / critical failure rate Are errors less frequent and less consequential? Total compute, wall-clock latency, and energy proxy Is the gain worth the resources? Cost per correct task completion Does orchestration improve efficiency? Error correlation and diversity contribution Do additional specialists add independent value? Examples/trials to competence on new tasks Is learning genuinely faster? Transfer gain to novel tasks Does earlier learning help later tasks? Forgetting / regression on older skills Was anything important damaged? Retained gain across sessions and versions Is learning persistent? Routing and organization contribution Did topology/policy improve outcomes beyond static baselines? Verification precision/recall and abstention Do checking and rejection help rather than merely slow work? No invented global HIVE score: Collect outcomes by task family, risk level, and budget before fitting a decision policy. Pareto trade-offs may be more informative than a single scalar rating. --- 6. HIVE information boundaries and contamination controls [SYNTHESIS / PREVIOUS-WORK] A specialist is not isolated simply because it uses another coding language, model, or memory format. Meaningful separation requires controls over who can read/write what, which claims cross a boundary, and under what verification standard. Boundary Candidate mechanism Protected against --------- Execution Separate processes, timeouts, resource quotas, sandboxing, restricted tools Crashes, uncontrolled actions, resource exhaustion Knowledge Local stores, access controls, provenance, epistemic-state flags Unverified claims becoming collective fact Communication Typed contracts, validation, translation, versioned schemas Representation mismatch, semantic contamination Model updates Versioned adapters/weights; offline tests; explicit promotion Cross-task interference and unreviewed parameter changes Organizational updates Controller candidate isolation, policy registry, rollback Bad global routing/topology changes Proposed message contract fields: message_id, source_agent, task_id, type (observationhypothesisproposaltest_resultverified_claim), payload_schema, evidence_refs, confidence_basis, validation_status, scope, permissions, timestamp, expiry, model_version, procedure_version. Important: These are design fields, not evidence that a particular transport or isolation method guarantees safety. --- 7. Alternative architectures to preserve Candidate Character Reason to test Primary risk ------------ ARCH-A Orchestrated specialists Controller/router, explicitly assigned workers, independent checks. Clear dependencies, auditability, predictable workflows. Central bottleneck, single controller error. ARCH-B Distributed collective Local rules, events/shared artifacts, distributed recruitment/selection. Parallel search and local responsiveness. Signal storms, premature convergence, attribution difficulty. ARCH-C Adaptive hybrid Central constraints + local independence + policy-controlled switching/blending. Potentially combines benefits of A and B for varying tasks. Complexity and overhead may exceed benefits. Hold the specialist set fixed during an initial architecture comparison where possible; otherwise improvements could be wrongly attributed to organizational policy. Also test a capable single-model-with-tools baseline under matched budget. --- 8. First experimental priorities (not completed) The highest-priority experiments measure organizational self-learning, not merely whether multi-agent output sounds sophisticated. Order Test A/B (or more) comparison Primary outcome ------------ EXP-01 Organization changes without weight changes Frozen models + static orchestration vs frozen models + adaptive organizational policy. Held-out quality and cost gain attributable to organization. EXP-02 Contextual switching vs always-on hybrid Fixed central, fixed distributed, always-on both, adaptive selector. Task-conditioned benefit net of routing overhead. EXP-03 Independent dissent and checking Single result vs majority vote vs independent evidence-checked proposals. Correctness, correlated errors, compute cost. EXP-04 Memory and contamination Unrestricted shared memory vs typed selective shared evidence + private working stores. Error propagation, task success, latency. EXP-05 Compounding future learning No retention vs retrieval-only vs procedural updates vs organizational updates. Examples/trials to competence on unfamiliar tasks. EXP-06 Rehearsal / consolidation No replay, interleaved replay, blocked replay, other clearly defined interventions. Retention, forgetting, transfer, resource cost. EXP-07 Dynamic group size One tool-equipped agent, several fixed agents, adaptive staffing. Correct tasks per resource and wall-clock. EXP-08 Hybrid specialists and software Generalist only vs specialists only vs specialist + deterministic software/checkers. End-to-end verified reliability and efficiency. Minimum evaluation requirements: seeded, reproducible workloads; task taxonomy; resource tracking; comparable tool/data access; held-out tests; ablations; explicit failed cases; versioned configurations; independent reference checks where feasible; rollback after regression. Suggested but unvalidated engineering thresholds from an earlier HIVE plan: ≥25% fewer examples to held-out competence; no more than 5 average percentage points and 10 on any one old-task benchmark of forgetting; no worse reliability than baseline; bounded cost. Treat these strictly as proposal-stage acceptance targets, not empirical discoveries or universal standards. --- 9. Open disputes: retain both views, do not silently resolve ID Views to preserve Current status / necessary test --------- DISP-01 Swarm/distributed control ↔ central orchestration Conditional design trade-off; run EXP-02. DISP-02 Consensus/majority ↔ competitive independent proposals Correlated errors and objective checking matter; run EXP-03. DISP-03 Common global memory ↔ protected specialist memory Typed, selective sharing is candidate compromise; run EXP-04. DISP-04 Shared model/backbone ↔ independent specialists/adapters Compare total cost, specialization gains, and interference on identical workloads. DISP-05 Natural-language messaging ↔ structured/latent translators Compare fidelity, throughput, interpretability and isolation; no assumed winner. DISP-06 Fully autonomous improvement ↔ governed changes Default to evaluated/versioned promotions until independent evidence supports less oversight. DISP-07 Many small experts ↔ a single larger workhorse Evaluate matched compute, tools and quality; neither wins universally. DISP-08 Continuous online adaptation ↔ periodic consolidation Test by change type and forgetting/latency cost. DISP-09 Tighter integration ↔ replaceability Tight coupling may aid some tasks but increases recovery/maintenance risk. DISP-10 Biological organizational analogy ↔ independently verified computation Use analogies to generate hypotheses, never to close empirical questions. DISP-11 Shared purpose ↔ plural independent dissent Preserve goal alignment without treating internal agreement as truth. DISP-12 One formula ↔ context-dependent formula families Current user direction prefers formula selection by framework; benchmark choice. Claims to quarantine or annotate - A larger group must be more intelligent. Unsupported; collaboration has measurable overhead and can decrease performance. - Several differently prompted/models must provide independent evidence. Unsupported without error-correlation measurement. - Passing an internal critic proves truth. Unsupported unless check validity/coverage is established. - Shared memory automatically becomes learning. False distinction; retention and behavioral improvement must be measured separately. - Evolutionary mutual dependence should make software modules irreversible. Misapplied analogy; replaceability is usually an engineering advantage. - Forest fungal networks are an established benevolent distributed intelligence. Contested/overstated in the research source. - Neural/global integration establishes artificial consciousness. Unresolved and separate from demonstrated task competence. - Immune receptor diversity estimates describe all receptors already present in one individual. Overgeneralized; theoretical and realized diversity must be distinguished. - Spiritual, sociological, biological, and computational explanations have identical causal mechanisms. Category error; use structural similarities without conflating meanings. - The biological/spiritual source's reported November 21, 2026 live checks were completed by November 20, 2026. Inconsistent provenance metadata; verify before reusing the claims as live-checked on that date. --- 10. Data ingestion, versioning, and provenance 10.1 Required record types Use separate records (or equivalent database tables) for: - Source — original file, paper, URL, original claim, retrieval/verification status, publication date. - Principle — normalized principle ID, precise meaning, domain, supporting sources, boundaries. - Finding — observation or conclusion with evidence class and possible falsifiers. - Design decision — decision ID, who/what authorized it, status, options retained. - Hypothesis — expected benefit, mechanism, conditions, risks, test plan. - Experiment — protocol, models, fixed resources, seed, baseline, outcome, result files, regressions. - Policy/formula — inputs, objective, assumptions, version, context, thresholds, evidence. - Failure/contradiction — case, provenance, severity, replication, unresolved explanations. 10.2 Suggested decision record yaml id: DEC-ORG-BOTH-001 title: Adaptive organizational duality status: selected_provisional_direction origin: user_discussion_2026-11-20 assertion: "Preserve both sides of most organization trade-offs; combine, switch, or blend contextually." constraints: - preserve_independent_disagreement - do_not_activate_every_mode_unconditionally - compare_to_simpler_matched_budget_baselines - require_independent_evaluation_before_promotion alternatives_retained: - fixed_central - fixed_distributed - always_on_hybrid - adaptive_selector implemented: false validated: false linked_experiments: [EXP-01, EXP-02] 10.3 Suggested experiment record yaml id: EXP-01 question: Does adaptive organization help with frozen specialist weights? status: proposed fixed: - specialist_models_and_versions - tool_access - evaluation_tasks_and_data - compute_budget_where_comparable independent_variable: organizational_policy dependent_variables: - held_out_task_success - cost_per_correct_completion - latency - regression_rate baselines: - capable_single_model_plus_tools - static_multi_agent_pipeline hypothesis: adaptive_policy_improves_net_performance result: null provenance_required: true 10.4 Merge rules 1. Append, do not erase contradictory theories or historical unsuccessful methods. 2. Cite original sources and distinguish their claims from HIVE translations and user choices. 3. Treat the two Organizational Principles of Multi-Agent Systems uploads as duplicate copies, not independent confirmations (identical file hashes in this environment). 4. Add backlinks using the actual document names below; create new pages only if the vault lacks those records. 5. Mark every speculative mechanism as proposed until its experiment has reported results. 6. A change to the working system needs a named baseline, metric, version, regression test, and rollback path. --- 11. Research index and source links Files to link inside Obsidian / knowledge base - [[HIVE_Consolidated_Organizational_Principles_and_Discrepancies]] — source consolidation and discrepancy ledger; the principal predecessor to this packet. - [[Organizational Principles of Multi-Agent Systems]] — computational five-cluster research. - [[Organizational Principles of Multi-Agent Systems (1)]] — duplicate; retain only if preserving upload provenance. - [[Spiritual and Biological Organizational Principles]] — biology/spirituality comparative source; analogies and empirical claims must remain distinguished. - [[HIVE_Framework_and_Research_Plan]] — prior topic/subtopic research approach and competing options (if present in vault). - [[HIVE_Build_Plan_and_Source_Foundation]] — previous build decisions and early learning constraints (if present in vault).
